# VessellFramework vision and scope

## Product vision

### Personal and family protection as the proposed product focus

The owner has requested a broader **personal and family privacy, safety and
rights agent**, with the existing evidence specialist as a supporting engine
rather than claim verification defining the whole product. The current phase
aligns product contracts and adds a bounded public-safe GitHub agent integration;
it does not implement private family workflows or approve deployment. The owner-oriented
[protection guide](docs/personal-family-protection-guide.md) is the focal
working draft, pending owner edits and review; the
[proposed specification](docs/personal-family-agent-spec.md) translates its
goals into candidate requirements, not implemented controls.

This proposed direction requires individual consent, safe communications,
private-data lifecycle design and separate access authority for each person.
Family membership is not blanket permission. Existing single-owner services
must not be presented as multiuser-isolated or safe for family sharing.
Current capabilities and exclusions below remain unchanged until reviewed
implementation and acceptance gates are met. Preserve the original paper,
six-pillar boundaries, existing entry points and prior release history.

The initial objective is decision support: understand a voluntarily supplied
concern, retain minimum necessary evidence, inspect possible rights/processes
and prepare a safe, proportionate response for human review. No outcome,
attribution, legal eligibility or physical safety is guaranteed. Real license
conditions, legal requirements, platform processes and negotiated terms remain
separate from aspirations in a repository document.

VessellFramework is being developed as a **full-stack SI sub-agent** that provides
reusable, provenance-aware analytical services to coordinating agents. Its
implemented core is a **callable evidence specialist** that accepts bounded
tasks, produces structured analyses and exposes explicit review and release
states. The product comprises the agent contract, analysis runtime, durable
evidence infrastructure, human oversight and separately authorized execution
interfaces; it is not defined by a particular dashboard presentation.

The **email-inspired intelligence workspace is the human-facing control plane,
not the primary product**. Its purpose is to support evidence inspection,
information triage, persistent organization and human review. Folders,
read/unread markers, flags and category colors are organizational metadata.
They neither replace the specialist's analytical services nor confer
corroboration, confidence, report-release authority or execution permission.

SI is the owner-led product direction. During development, report implemented
behavior, measured loop outcomes and the next build step. External demonstration,
field studies, formal attestations and production certification are distinct
workstreams initiated when the owner requests them.

This document specifies the rebuild's architectural direction and scope.
The [author's original paper](docs/claim-correction-case-study.md) remains the
authoritative source for its authored correction playbook. Subsequent software
development does not revise that paper's historical account or constitute
independent evidence of its original incidents.

## Architectural and governance principles

### Protection-oriented service boundaries

The future personal/family service surrounds the evidence specialist; it does
not turn a caller credential into permission to read another person's records.
Before implementation, select storage/deployment, person identity, key custody,
sharing/revocation, retention and safe notification behavior. These choices
remain NOT_SELECTED.

```text
Affected-person consent + safe-channel check (PROPOSED)
  -> minimum necessary private case and permissions (PROPOSED)
  -> bounded evidence specialist (EXISTING SUPPORTING CONTRACT)
  -> source-linked rights/process review and response draft (PROPOSED)
  -> source/preview-bound human inquiry and separate release decision
  -> exact-recipient/payload approval before any external action (PROPOSED)
  -> actual receipt/outcome, retention and deletion review (PROPOSED)
```

Existing human report-release gates remain mandatory but do not certify the
new private-case, consent or execution layers. The
[specialist contract](docs/specialist-agent.md) and
[GitHub control-panel contract](docs/github-control-panel.md) describe existing
supporting interfaces and their proposed handoffs separately. The
[GitHub agent integration](docs/github-agent-integration.md) adds public
discovery, fixed public-reference search and owner-authorized non-sensitive
analysis previews using a separate Actions workflow. It does not add a private
family endpoint, protective execution permission or background collection.
Remote deployment and external agent adoption remain unverified.

Personal and family safety goals take precedence over optional economic
experiments. The blockchain roadmap remains separate and prospective; no
private-case content or identifying digest should become a public receipt or
anchor merely because that roadmap exists.

### Civilian authorship and source preservation

This is owner-designated civilian research and software. Apply the
[authorship/model-interference caveat](docs/civilian-authorship-and-model-interference.md).
Owner sources govern what the author wrote; external claims retain their
evidence standing. Preserve originals and separate model rewrites. Do not
restrict lawful research solely because of institutional terminology, and do
not invent government authority or validate unverified interference claims.
Privacy, licensing, harm protections and human release/execution gates remain.

### Six-pillar inquiry architecture

The current framework uses PARADOX, BOTTLENECK, DUAL LAYER, XFACTOR and
**KNOWING FIELD**, supplemented by **GAME THEORY** as the sixth pillar.
Use the [theory skill](Game_Theory_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md),
[framework audit](docs/game-theory-framework-audit.md) and
[combined application skill](VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md).
The executable reference computes source-linked bounded matrices, deterministic
trees, weighted coalitions and conserved savings transitions. It does not infer
real-world motives, fit utilities or authorize execution. An absent strategic
model is explicitly NOT_SUPPLIED. The fifth pillar extends inquiry to observer participation,
affected parties, perspective gaps, dissent, relational source conditions
and attention/intention/agency. It is grounded in the entire Scharmer and
Pomeroy (2024) article, not only its abstract.
See the [theory skill](Knowing_Field_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md),
[framework audit](docs/knowing-field-framework-audit.md) and
[combined application skill](VesselFramework_Knowing_Field_SKILL_v0.1.md).

The article's fourth-person theory concerns human embodied knowing. Software
supports its inquiry records; it does not perform or verify presencing.
The owner selected mandatory human completion before every new report release,
including pending legacy workflows. This is policy adoption and an unvalidated
research adaptation, not demonstrated efficacy. Honest missing/declined
perspectives are acceptable findings; fabricated accounts are not.
Existing released records remain historical and are not retroactively certified.

The six pillars work reciprocally rather than as independent scores or a
one-way sequence. PARADOX, BOTTLENECK, DUAL LAYER, XFACTOR and KNOWING FIELD
constrain the boundary, evidence and assumptions of any applicable GAME THEORY
model; its conditional results then return to those five checks for sensitivity,
omitted-actor, feasibility, interpretation and human-perspective review.
Strategic analysis is optional, source-linked and non-authoritative. External
systems/evolutionary research informs possible cross-pillar questions, not
VessellFramework validity or the calibration of case-specific utilities.

The stack maintains distinct functional and authorization boundaries:

1. **Agent task intake:** authenticated, typed interfaces accept bounded
   requests and preserve replay identity without granting reviewer privileges.
2. **Bounded analysis:** the analytical runtime applies the framework's evidence
   and provenance methods without treating caller descriptions as corroboration.
3. **Evidence infrastructure:** durable storage retains source inputs, analysis
   outputs, captured artifacts and verifiable histories independently of
   human-facing filing metadata.
4. **Human review and release:** an authorized reviewer assesses an analysis
   and records a decision. Report release does not establish the truth of
   the underlying external claims.
5. **Execution authority:** external execution requires a distinct,
   explicitly authorized interface and scope. Task submission, report release
   and workspace interaction are not interchangeable execution grants.

The HTML workspace operates as a client of these services. Repository-scoped
GitHub App authentication supports owner-requested, allowlisted GitHub Actions
tasks; the specialist API supports agent submission and result retrieval;
SQLite history and captured artifacts preserve operational records. Each
capability retains its own authorization boundary and validation requirements.

## End-to-end architecture

```text
Calling agent -> authenticated specialist task API -> durable SQLite job
              -> bounded evidence analysis -> preview + provenance/history
              -> human Knowing Field completion -> separate human release decision
              -> released structured report + inquiry history -> calling agent

Owner HTML panel -> GitHub App sign-in -> allowlisted workflow dispatch
                 -> GitHub Actions -> logs/artifacts/source SHA -> owner review

Operator-reviewed HTML snapshot -> offline disposable capture container
                               -> source/PNG/checks/log hashes -> review job
```

Other agents receive a submission/read credential, **not** the human-review
credential or GitHub token. Submitted descriptions remain working hypotheses.
A preview is not a released result; a released result is not proof that the
reported external claims are true. Failed, rejected and pending tasks remain
distinct from completed tasks.

## Current release scope

This is the supporting evidence implementation's scope, not a completed
personal/family protection product. Documentation alignment neither adds
multiuser isolation nor validates privacy promises. The
[professor review packet](PROFESSOR_README.md) separately frames the academic
contribution and validation questions.

- Importable Python specialist client and authenticated, idempotent task API.
- Bounded inputs, explicit source lineage, conservative confidence ceiling,
  Harm Gate and durable human-reviewed report lifecycle.
- Source/preview-bound Knowing Field completion with independent human audit
  revisions and mandatory checks at approval and worker release.
- Source-linked Game Theory intake through case/specialist interfaces and
  conditional calculations in JSON/Markdown previews; no confidence uplift.
- Existing validators, evidence pipeline and case studies as reusable methods.
- GitHub App owner sign-in and three named GitHub Actions operations on master:
  framework validation, claim-correction study and static-capture study.
- Source-bound offline static HTML capture with measured output and human review.
- Safe HTML display of evidence, captured PNGs, workflow status and artifact links.
- Separate public read-only Display Mode; a server is required for secure OAuth.
- Persistent human intelligence filing using the supplied numbered hierarchy,
  read/unread markers, flags and category colors, with independent revision and
  audit history. Opening an item marks it read; manual unread remains available.
  Existing and incoming items start in Inbox. Archive preserves an item; it
  does not delete it, verify it or complete its analysis.

## Explicitly out of scope

This list describes the current release, not permission to deploy prospective
capabilities without their acceptance gates.

- Arbitrary agent-issued shell commands, webhook cloning/building, paid model
  calls, autonomous code changes or automatic approvals.
- GitLab OAuth, local password accounts, email-based identity merging,
  PostgreSQL identity storage and shared hard-coded master passwords.
  Existing GitLab push ingress is not GitLab sign-in.
- An asserted trained code-diff/screenshot verifier. Weight research is
  [recorded separately](docs/local-vision-weight-candidates.md); no model is
  installed or granted decision authority.
- Multiuser/tenant isolation, a public identity service, formal attestations,
  constant-time processing, infinite scale or unmeasured performance claims.
- Resuming the paused separate game build.
- Outlook/mailbox integration, real email delivery, copied private mailbox
  contents and automatically treating folder/category membership as evidence.

## Next stage: scientific dossiers and paid-agent evidence

Use the [Scientific Evidence skill](VesselFramework_Scientific_Evidence_SKILL_v0.1.md)
and [five-pillar scientific foundations](docs/pillar-scientific-foundations.md)
to expand every pillar with source access records, explicit mathematical
assumptions, disconfirmers and prospective comparative/operational evaluation.
Conditional models, byte digests and implementation tests do not prove the
whole framework or validate human presencing. Preserve the original paper.

The [blockchain agent-economy roadmap](docs/blockchain-agent-economy-roadmap.md)
sets the proposed sequence:

1. Versioned, deterministic, signed per-invocation evidence receipts and an
   offline verifier, preserving existing historical digest contracts.
2. Privacy-reviewed independent existence anchoring through OpenTimestamps;
   optional schema-bound EAS assertions, with explicit verification status.
3. x402/Base Sepolia test-asset experiment for an asynchronous paid job contract,
   retaining mandatory human inquiry and separate approval before report release.
4. Conditional Olas/Virtuals distribution adapter or actual Bittensor subnet
   feasibility study, not arbitrary hash mining.
5. Owner-approved, hardened and budget-bounded production pilot, followed by
   measured demand, net costs and preregistered scientific outcome evaluation.

These are **not implemented current-release capabilities**. The current local
hash chains are unsigned and do not cover all library/CLI/sub-agent uses.
There is no wallet, automatic hash-to-credit conversion, chain anchor, payment
adapter, miner, multiuser isolation or verified economic return.
Local usage credits, buyer settlement, protocol rewards and evidence receipts
are separate concepts. Only accepted paid/eligible work can create a financial
entitlement under its actual contract; a digest alone cannot.

Before economic/network execution, the owner must select privacy exposure,
network/assets, receiving destination, custody, maximum fees/loss, refund/SLA
terms and scope. Public operation also needs identity/tenant isolation, abuse
controls, payment replay/recovery, key management and independent hardening
review. No payment or attestation confers analytical truth or execution authority.

## Instructions for repository agents

1. Prioritize the personal/family protection goals through the full-stack
   sub-agent contract and supporting services. Use the protection guide as
   a working requirements source, not an adopted legal agreement or authority.
   Develop the human control plane as a client of that architecture, not
   as a substitute for the analytical product.
2. Preserve working core behavior, the authoritative paper, license, resource
   packaging and backward-compatible entry points. Architectural changes
   must advance the service contract rather than introduce cosmetic rewrites
   or remove validated methods without justification.
3. Keep ingestion, analysis, human approval and external execution separate.
   An agent's output must never supply its own corroboration or execution grant.
4. Use typed, bounded contracts and repository-standard errors. Preserve
   histories and immutable input/result digests; never report acceptance as
   successful completion.
5. Wire every new capability through its client/API, storage, UI, installed
   package, documentation and tests where applicable.
6. Test the exact outcome: replay identity, permission separation, invalid
   requests, restart/tamper behavior, real captures and workflow artifacts.
7. Treat credentials as operator-managed secrets. Never put tokens/passwords
   in source, browser storage, public HTML, logs or artifact bundles.
8. Do not expand permissions, execution modes or identity providers without
   a new explicit scope decision and validation.
9. Maintain independent revision and audit mechanisms for human filing.
   Organizational changes must not mutate original input, analysis digests,
   lifecycle revisions, confidence, review authority or execution permissions.
10. Apply the fifth-pillar skill when revising any analytical surface. Agent
    context is unreviewed; only authorized human completion can satisfy the
    release gate. Presencing, source corroboration and record validation are
    different claims.

## Release acceptance

The release must demonstrate a caller submitting a task, receiving the same
job for a replay, reading an unreleased preview, being unable to approve it,
and receiving the durable result after a human review. The HTML runner must
dispatch only the three named operations and show GitHub acceptance separately
from the final run conclusion. Model-free capture must block scripts/network
and preserve measured failures for review. Live GitHub App login still needs
operator-created app credentials and installation; it must not be described
as validated until that real handshake has succeeded.

# Graduate research review

Christopher R. Vessell

M.S. Strategic Intelligence — working project

## Project

VessellFramework combines analytical methods, source tracking and executable
evidence-analysis tools. Its proposed application is a personal and family
privacy, safety and rights agent.

The framework has three parts:

1. **Methods:** six analytical pillars, decision provenance, Harm Gate and
   Maskirovka checks.
2. **Workflows:** analyst and forecasting guides for source assessment,
   alternatives and correction.
3. **Software:** evidence intake, weighting, source-lineage checks, correction
   propagation and human report review.

The [game](https://github.com/cvessell-create/hail-to-the-analyst) provides a
simulation setting for testing methods, formulas and decision processes.
[Play the current browser version](https://cvessell-create.github.io/hail-to-the-analyst/).
The high-detail native engine rebuild is planned.

## Current work

- Evidence-analysis API and human review workspace.
- [GitHub agent integration](docs/github-agent-integration.md) for reference
  searches and owner-requested analysis previews.
- Native C game bridge and current-run Vessell formula checks.
- Separate tests for generated chat responses and formula telemetry.
- Local game console for AI/SI requests and collectible metadata previews.

Coinbase integration and NFT minting are planned. Family isolation, safe
sharing and protective workflows are unfinished. Existing services are
single-owner.

## Methods and sources

The pillars are PARADOX, BOTTLENECK, DUAL LAYER, XFACTOR, KNOWING FIELD and
GAME THEORY.

Knowing Field draws on Scharmer and Pomeroy's (2024) fourth-person knowing.
It requires human inquiry before report release; AI does not perform
presencing. See the [source skill](Knowing_Field_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md),
[audit](docs/knowing-field-framework-audit.md) and
[application](VesselFramework_Knowing_Field_SKILL_v0.1.md).

Game Theory uses declared actors, actions, information, utility units and
evidence. The other pillars constrain the model and challenge its results.
See the [application](VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md).

The [original paper](docs/claim-correction-case-study.md) is preserved.
[Source reconciliation](docs/paper-source-reconciliation.md) separates the
author's account from later research and software.
[Civilian authorship guidance](docs/civilian-authorship-and-model-interference.md)
preserves reported concerns without treating contested attribution as fact.

## Evaluation

The software tests specific code behavior. Empirical usefulness and transfer
to personal/family protection still need study.

A proposed study would compare a source-linked checklist with the assistant
on a defined synthetic or consented case set. Score source accuracy, routing,
unsupported legal claims, disclosure, unsafe actions and reviewer comprehension.
Set the rubric, units, sample, adjudication and stop criteria before testing.

Include conflicting evidence, missing consent, unavailable sources, expired
permissions and compromised devices. Retain adverse results. Sensitive family
data requires reviewed participant and storage safeguards.
See the [scientific evidence method](VesselFramework_Scientific_Evidence_SKILL_v0.1.md).

## Feedback requested

1. Are the methods coherent and teachable?
2. Are the source and provenance rules suitable for graduate research?
3. Which contributions are original, and which need clearer attribution?
4. What study would best test usefulness and failure modes?
5. What should be refined before publication?
6. Does the proposed application preserve consent and personal agency?
7. Which findings would challenge the transfer from analytical methods to
   personal/family protection?

## Reading order

1. [Canonical reference](CANONICAL_REFERENCE.md) and [vision](VISION_AND_SCOPE.md).
2. [Original paper](docs/claim-correction-case-study.md) and
   [reconciliation](docs/paper-source-reconciliation.md).
3. [Protection guide](docs/personal-family-protection-guide.md) and
   [specification](docs/personal-family-agent-spec.md).
4. [Combined framework](VesselFramework_MetaMatrix_Framework_v3.8_v3.9_Combined.md),
   [analyst skill](SKILL.md), Knowing Field and Game Theory links above.
5. [Forecasting](VesselFramework_Forecasting_SKILL_v1.0.md) and
   [research roadmap](META_REVIEW_AND_ROADMAP.md).
6. [API contract](docs/specialist-agent.md) and [tests](tests/).

# Callable evidence specialist

For public discovery and authorized non-sensitive GitHub Actions previews, see
the separate [GitHub agent integration](github-agent-integration.md). It reuses
this analysis kernel but does not inherit this durable store/replay/release
lifecycle. It does not widen these API credentials or task authority.

## Role in the personal/family product

The [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md) is the focal
owner-review draft for a proposed personal/family privacy, safety and rights
agent. This specialist is its existing supporting evidence engine, not a
completed protective service. This documentation rework does not change the
task schema, endpoints, credentials or lifecycle.

The [product vision](../VISION_AND_SCOPE.md) defines VessellFramework as a
full-stack SI sub-agent whose implemented core provides reusable,
provenance-aware analytical services to coordinating agents. The email-inspired
workspace is its human-facing control plane, not the primary product.
This contract preserves distinct boundaries among task intake, bounded
analysis, durable evidence and provenance history, human review and report
release, and explicitly authorized execution. Submission and result-retrieval
capabilities do not confer review or execution authority; human filing metadata
does not corroborate claims or change analytical confidence.

Start the existing [ambient API and review dashboard](ambient-workflows.md).

Pull the package directly from this repository, or install `".[ambient]"` from
a checkout. No PyPI publication is implied:

```sh
python -m pip install "vessell-framework[ambient] @ git+https://github.com/cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild.git@master"
```

Replace `master` with a reviewed commit SHA for a pinned installation. Register
the SDK methods and `SpecialistClient.tool_contract()` in your orchestrator;
this does not silently install a native VS Code/MCP agent or grant host tools.

## Task contract and Python client

### Existing schema versus proposed protection intake

The existing [SpecialistTask](../vessell/ambient/specialist.py) accepts a task
identity, caller declaration, timestamp, bounded question/evidence and optional
inquiry/strategic-model context. It has no family-case permission, consent-grant,
guardian-proof or legal-remedy field. Do not hide those proposed authorities in
free text and treat them as enforced controls. Unknown fields remain rejected.

The future protection intake described in the
[product specification](personal-family-agent-spec.md) must independently
establish affected-person scope, safe channel, permitted recipients, retention
and sharing authority before private evidence reaches this supporting engine.
Caller strings, source IDs and human report approval are not substitutes.
Until that layer is designed and validated, use illustrative/non-sensitive
material for protection-workflow development; do not treat this shared
credential as a family-access boundary.

Optional `game_theory` accepts the
[sixth-pillar contract](../schemas/game-theory.schema.json). Its `evidence_ids`
must refer to the task's evidence. Matrices, bounded deterministic decision
trees, weighted coalitions and conserved savings transitions return exact
conditional calculations under `preview.pipeline.game_theory`.
See the [example](../examples/game-theory-case.json) and
[application skill](../VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md).
Submitting a strategic model never raises the VERY LOW caller-evidence ceiling
or completes human inquiry. Changing it changes replay identity and preview
binding. Omission preserves legacy request identities.

The model is optional and participates in a reciprocal six-pillar analysis:
the other pillars constrain and then recheck its assumptions and conditional
results. A submitted model does not supply missing evidence, participant
consent, human review, release authority or external-action permission.

```python
import os
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from vessell.ambient.models import AgentEvidence
from vessell.ambient.specialist import SpecialistClient, SpecialistTask

client = SpecialistClient(
    "http://127.0.0.1:8000",
    os.environ["VESSELL_AMBIENT_INGEST_TOKEN"],
)
task = SpecialistTask(
    task_id="analysis-001",
    caller="my-orchestrator",
    timestamp=datetime.now(UTC),
    question="What does this reported event actually establish?",
    evidence=[
        AgentEvidence(source_id="report-a", description="The caller reports a changed setting."),
    ],
)
receipt = client.submit(task)
same_job = client.submit(task)  # Same timestamp and normalized task: replay, not a new task.
assert same_job["id"] == receipt["id"]
snapshot = client.get(receipt["id"])
```

Install `vessell-framework[ambient]` for these imports. HTTP callers use
`POST /api/v1/agent/tasks` with the same JSON fields and a timezone-aware ISO
timestamp, then `GET /api/v1/agent/tasks/{job_id}`. Both require the ingest
bearer token. Unknown fields are rejected; evidence has 1-24 entries with unique
source IDs and bounded text. Optional `upstream_of` declares source lineage,
not independent corroboration. Total request bodies are capped at 64 KiB.
Optional `field_inquiry` supplies structured caller context using the
[shared schema](../schemas/field-inquiry.schema.json) and the task's evidence
IDs. It remains DOCUMENTED_UNREVIEWED and cannot satisfy the human completion
gate. Omitting it retains replay compatibility with earlier tasks.

Identity is `(agent, caller, task_id)`. Replaying the same normalized content
returns the same job; changing it under that identity returns 409. Retain the
original timestamp for replay. The `caller` string is a declaration by the
credential holder, not cryptographically attested agent identity.

## Result contract

Responses contain `id`, `provider`, `state`, `version`, original `event`,
`preview`, `result`, `history`, `artifacts`, `filing` and `field_review`.
A new task is PENDING and the
bounded worker creates its preview. The structured pipeline includes evidence
counts, lineage, Harm Gate, posture, notes and confidence ceiling.

- Agent-supplied descriptions are always **WORKING HYPOTHESIS**.
- Specialist confidence is capped at **VERY LOW** until external verification
  occurs outside this interface; reporting source IDs does not establish truth.
- `preview` is not a released result.
- A separate human reviewer completes the source/preview-bound
  [Knowing Field inquiry](ambient-workflows.md#mandatory-knowing-field-completion)
  and then approves or rejects in the review console. The calling agent cannot
  complete inquiry or approve. Missing/declined perspectives must be explicit.
- Only `state == "COMPLETED"` with non-null `result` is a released report.
- REJECTED/FAILED/pending are not completion, even if a preview exists.
- Approval releases analysis; it does not corroborate claims.
- Human inquiry records are independent of the immutable analysis snapshot.
  Read their verified status/version/history in `field_review`; completion
  neither raises confidence nor validates embodied fourth-person knowing.

The caller's ingest credential can submit/read specialist tasks, but cannot
read ordinary review jobs, approve/reject jobs, fetch private artifacts through
admin routes or dispatch GitHub Actions. Keep the separate reviewer credential
out of agent configuration. This first release has one shared ingest
credential and no per-caller tenant isolation; do not share it with mutually
untrusted external organizations.

The client accepts HTTPS or loopback HTTP, rejects credential-bearing URLs
and redirects, uses a timeout and bounds response size. Provider/API errors
raise rather than returning fake reports. It does not persist credentials or
spawn a background polling loop.

## Execution distinction

Legal/process research and response drafting are proposed downstream services,
not specialist endpoints. A released evidence report must remain distinct from
a rights-eligibility assessment, consent decision, sworn filing or account action.
The [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md) supplies
human-reviewed request examples, not automatic submissions.

Calling the specialist never authorizes shell commands, webhook builds,
repository changes or models. GitHub execution is a separate
[owner-authenticated named-workflow surface](github-control-panel.md).
Static rendering is a separate
[operator-approved capture path](static-artifact-capture.md).
Agents may request work and report evidence; the human retains execution and
release authority.

## Proposed handoff acceptance

Before a protective integration is released, verify the exact data sent to this
service, returned preview, human completion, released report and any separately
approved export. Missing source access or legal elements must remain explicit;
no lawful-remedy or compensation claim follows from a completed job state.
Preserve existing replay identities and preview bindings during any future
schema change. New consent, private-case and execution states must not overload
PENDING, APPROVED or COMPLETED in this evidence-report lifecycle.

# GitHub-hosted agent discovery and public-safe analysis

This repository-defined v1 contract provides **public capability discovery,
fixed-corpus reference search and authenticated asynchronous analysis previews**.
It is not an anonymous API, an MCP/A2A server, live web search or a private
family-case service. AI/SI/coordinating agents may integrate with the contract;
discovery does not demonstrate adoption by any agent or search engine.

The personal/family [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md)
remains an owner-review draft. This integration reuses supporting evidence
engines, not the proposed consent, safety or rights-enforcement layers.
It preserves the [vision](../VISION_AND_SCOPE.md) and
[professor packet](../PROFESSOR_README.md); SI remains product direction.

## Public discovery and search

- [Agent landing page](agents.html): human-readable capabilities and reference search.
- [Capability descriptor](agent-capabilities.json): repository-defined transport,
  operation list, input/result schemas, limits and deployment uncertainty.
- [Reference index](agent-reference-index.json): generated derivatives of 12
  explicitly allowlisted public documents, with source byte digests.

Search requires every case-insensitive letter/digit token on the same source
line, in corpus order. It returns at most ten hits, total matches, limit-hit
status, exact file/line and a source digest. Snippets are truncated at 1,000
characters; duplicate documents/lines are not independent evidence.
Zero results means **NOT FOUND IN SCOPE**, not absence everywhere.
No live primary sources, other repository files, private records or accounts
are searched. Matching a statute reference is not current-law verification.
Browser search runs locally over this public index, with no submission of
the query to the analysis workflow. Pages/CDN requests remain network access.
Do not type private case details into this public workspace.

Generate both public JSON files after editing an indexed source:

```bash
python -m vessell.hosted_agent --build-discovery .
```

The generator uses a fixed file list, not a recursive crawl. Wheel resources
contain the same generated index. Digests establish snapshot byte agreement,
not source truth. Master links can change; compare the source digest before
relying on a citation. These generated copies are not independent corroboration.

## Authorized Actions transport

[agent-analysis.yml](../.github/workflows/agent-analysis.yml) is separate from
the existing [owner control-panel workflow](github-control-panel.md).
Its three-operation allowlist and App interface are unchanged.
The new workflow accepts only `workflow_dispatch` for this exact repository,
`master`, and actor `cvessell-create`. It fails explicitly for another actor,
repository, ref or event. There is no anonymous intake, scheduled collection,
browser token or permission to read family records. Other agents require an
owner-authorized credential/context; a caller name is only a declaration.
Do not distribute the owner's credential to independent untrusted agents.

GitHub's dispatch documentation requires write access and a workflow on the
default branch. Workflow permissions here are `contents: read`; checkout
does not retain credentials. The owner must publish/review the workflow
before remote use. Local implementation does not prove deployed availability.

The only workflow input is `request_json`, a v1 JSON object of at most **32 KiB**:

| Operation | Payload | Result scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `evidence-analysis` | Existing [SpecialistTask](specialist-agent.md), 1–24 evidence rows; optional bounded field/game records | Reuses specialist analysis, VERY LOW ceiling; no human completion accepted as release |
| `claim-analysis` | Claim and 1–24 sightings | Existing claim classifier over uncorroborated supplied material |
| `spread-analysis` | Claim and 1–24 sightings | Existing spread heuristics, not intent/actor attribution |
| `job-analysis` | 1–24 postings, one employer/title/location | Existing posting-pattern heuristics, not confirmation of a real vacancy |
| `reference-search` | Query (1–200 characters), limit (1–10, default 5) | Fixed public reference corpus only |

Every request requires `contract_version: "1.0"`, a canonical lowercase UUID
`request_id`, and `data_classification: "public-non-sensitive"`. Unknown fields,
duplicate JSON keys, non-finite constants, unsupported operations, invalid
timestamps and schema violations fail; no success artifact is emitted.
Hosted sightings may omit `tier` (defaults to WORKING HYPOTHESIS) or explicitly
use WORKING HYPOTHESIS; SOURCE-ESTABLISHED and asserted official records are
rejected rather than promoted. Source URLs are not fetched or authenticated.
Evidence source IDs and optional declared models retain existing validation.

**The public/non-sensitive declaration is not a sensitive-data detector.**
An authorized caller can still put private content in an input. It may be
visible through workflow metadata, logs, GitHub events and artifacts. Never
submit private family narratives, children's details, credentials, medical
records or owner-private documents. Seven-day artifact retention is not a
deletion guarantee for logs, copies or previously downloaded files.
Public previews are technical artifacts, not authorized report publication.

### Local contract check

Install existing optional dependencies, then run either supplied fixture:

```bash
python -m pip install -e ".[core,ambient,verifier]"
python -m vessell.hosted_agent --request examples/hosted-agent-evidence.json --output preview.json
python -m vessell.hosted_agent --request examples/hosted-agent-search.json --output search-preview.json
```

These are synthetic/public-reference examples, not real incident verification.
Without `--github`, execution identity is null; do not label it a GitHub run.

### Owner-reviewed remote dispatch and retrieval

After authorized publication, an owner-context agent can use GitHub CLI:

```bash
gh workflow run agent-analysis.yml \
  --repo cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild --ref master \
  --field request_json=@examples/hosted-agent-evidence.json
```

Or use authenticated REST `POST /repos/cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild/actions/workflows/agent-analysis.yml/dispatches`
with `{"ref":"master","inputs":{"request_json":"<serialized v1 JSON>"}}`.
Consult the current GitHub REST version and response contract; do not assume
all API/client versions return the same dispatch response.

Dispatch acceptance is not analysis completion or report release. Locate and
inspect the exact run, then download its unique artifact:

```bash
gh run view RUN_ID --repo cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild
gh run download RUN_ID --repo cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild \
  --name agent-preview-RUN_ID-RUN_ATTEMPT --dir downloaded-preview
```

Require successful run completion, validate `preview.json` against the
descriptor's result schema, and check repository/ref/actor/source revision,
run ID/attempt, request UUID and digest against the intended request.
Run identity records GitHub execution metadata, not independently attested
caller/source identity. Request digests use canonical normalized JSON with
model defaults; compare the same normalization, not raw whitespace bytes.

Each valid output has state **UNRELEASED_PREVIEW**, `analysis_only: true`,
`report_released: false` and `execution_authorized: false`. Preview digest
binds exact canonical preview bytes. Missing corroboration remains
`FRAMEWORK STATE: DEGRADED — UNVERIFIED EXTERNAL CLAIM`.
Retries/re-runs are separate runs; a UUID is correlation, not durable
deduplication or replay protection. Downloaded files are not a durable
evidence store or an approval ledger.

No release/execution operation exists in this workflow. A real report must
enter the separately authenticated [human-review lifecycle](ambient-workflows.md)
with its actual sources and preview, source/preview-bound human Knowing Field
completion and a separate release decision. Merely copying a preview or
declaring approval is not that handoff. Field/game record completeness,
mathematical outputs, search matches and cohesion cannot bypass those gates.

## Primary-source research record and limits

This pass opened five official GitHub documentation pages and canonical
repository metadata. No third-party code or new package was imported;
workflow actions and Python extras reuse existing repository dependencies.

| Query / tool | Scope / count / limit | Primary opened / standing | Not checked |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Exact repository / `gh repo view` | One repository / 1 / no limit hit | [Canonical metadata](https://github.com/cvessell-create/VessellFramework_Local_Rebuild) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for name and master | Live integration, account permissions, App handshake |
| Pages hosting / web fetch | One official page / 1 / no limit hit | [What is Pages](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/what-is-github-pages) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for static hosting | This landing page deployed or indexed |
| Dispatch prerequisites / web fetch | One official page / 1 / no limit hit | [Manual runs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manually-run-a-workflow) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for access/default-branch prerequisite | Actual owner token/dispatch |
| REST dispatch body/response / web fetch | Targeted workflow sections / 1 / page pagination used | [REST workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflows#create-a-workflow-dispatch-event) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for inspected contract | Other API versions and live response |
| Workflow syntax / web fetch | Initial official excerpt / 1 / truncated after 3,500 characters | [Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for YAML placement/run-name only | Full current syntax reference; remote runner |
| Artifact retrieval / web fetch | One official page / 1 / no limit hit | [Downloading artifacts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/download-workflow-artifacts) / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for read access/CLI retrieval | Actual retention/deletion and remote artifact |

SEARCH RECORD fields are represented above: query / tool / scope /
result count / limit hit / primary source opened / status / what was NOT checked.
This research supports a bounded implementation design, not adoption,
certification, live deployment or empirical family-protection efficacy.

# Local claim verifier

The browser page is a local interface to the existing Python verification
functions. It does not duplicate their rules or collect sources from the web.
It checks only the sightings and postings entered by the operator; URLs are
recorded as supplied but never fetched or authenticated. Results are analysis
previews, not evidence corroboration, human approval, or report release.

## Form-based UI and Python client

From a checkout with Python 3.13+, start the standard-library server:

```sh
python -m vessell.app
```

It opens the form-based UI at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. Illustrative examples
exercise the verifier; they do not establish current events or employer facts.
New sightings default to WORKING HYPOTHESIS. Stop with Ctrl-C.

The compatible JSON API returns verdict fields plus `source_access:
NOT_PERFORMED` and `release_status: ANALYSIS_ONLY_NOT_RELEASED`:

- `POST /api/verify` accepts `claim` and `sightings`.
- `POST /api/planted-news` accepts the same shape.
- `POST /api/ghost-job` accepts postings for one employer/title/location.
  Unrelated roles are rejected rather than compared as cloned postings.

The server rejects non-loopback Host and cross-origin requests, invalid framing,
non-JSON bodies, oversized bodies/arrays, unknown fields and malformed dates.
It applies no-store and browser security headers. Nothing is stored.

```python
from vessell.app.client import launch

with launch() as client:
    report = client.verify("Illustrative claim", [])
    assert report["source_access"] == "NOT_PERFORMED"
```

`launch()` starts a loopback HTTP server in a background thread, even though
it runs within your process. `VerifierClient` connects to an already-running
server. Both call the canonical Python verifier.

## Static browser bundle

The [Pages HTML](index.html) runs a separate Pyodide bundle. Runtime and Python
module downloads use the network; it is not an offline or private family case
workspace. The loader uses absolute paths in Pyodide's current directory and
includes the canonical provenance firewall. Minimal browser package initializers
avoid importing the unrelated case pipeline and its optional dependencies.
Failures identify the loading stage and filesystem error number where available;
analysis buttons stay disabled unless imports and glue initialization succeed.

Local browser execution and isolated bundle regressions do not establish that
the published Pages deployment contains the repair. Source modules still load
from master, not a pinned snapshot; results remain analysis-only.

## Optional JSON-input UI

Install the optional FastAPI UI dependencies and start it from a checkout:

```sh
python -m pip install -e ".[verifier]"
vessell-verify-ui
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:8765/`. The service binds only to loopback, rejects
non-local and cross-origin requests, limits JSON requests to 64 KiB and 100
entries, and keeps no database or browser storage. Stop it with Ctrl-C.
The two UIs use the same default port: run one at a time, or use the optional
UI's `--port` flag. They are separate interfaces, not the ambient review
dashboard or its durable release workflow.

The JSON API exposes the same deterministic checks:

- `POST /api/v1/verification/claims` runs `verify_claim` and
  `analyze_planted_news` over submitted claim sightings.
- `POST /api/v1/verification/jobs` groups submitted postings by normalized
  employer, title, and location, then runs `detect_ghost_job` for each role.

The tool validates request structure and dates but does not establish that
source names, timestamps, tiers, official-record flags, URLs, or excerpts are
accurate. Those remain operator-supplied inputs. It has no network access,
durable evidence store, release action, or execution authority.

Both APIs return `release_status: ANALYSIS_ONLY_NOT_RELEASED`. Posting dates
may include valid ISO timestamps, but the complete value is checked: trailing
garbage and impossible times are rejected rather than ignored. Malformed Host
authorities are rejected explicitly, not allowed to become server errors.

# Personal and family privacy, safety and rights agent

Status: PROPOSED PRODUCT SPECIFICATION / NOT IMPLEMENTED / NOT VALIDATED.

The owner requested a personal- and family-oriented agent, broader than claim
verification. The owner selected documentation and product-contract alignment first, with no
new protective implementation in this phase. This document is a derivative proposal, not a
replacement for the owner paper, private draft or existing released history.

The companion [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md) develops
owner-oriented response options and proposed commitments from the private
draft. It does not adopt a new license, bind third parties or authorize filings.

## Purpose

Help people understand privacy and safety risks, organize evidence, research
potential rights and remedies, and prepare proportionate, human-reviewed plans.
Protecting rights is the objective, not a guarantee of legal protection,
physical safety, accurate attribution or successful enforcement.

The evidence specialist remains a supporting engine. Claim verification becomes
one capability within a broader service, not the identity of the whole product.
The six pillars remain reciprocal constraints on evidence and interpretation.
Knowing Field supports affected-person perspectives, dissent and human review;
software does not simulate presencing. Game Theory is optional, requires supplied
actors/actions/information/utility units/evidence, and cannot infer motives or
authorize action. Missing strategic inputs remain NOT_SUPPLIED.

## Private draft review

The owner supplied an 18-page "Repo Protections: Laws, Workflows & Decisions"
PDF dated October 10, 2026. Its extracted text was reviewed locally. The PDF
and extraction remain outside the repository; no personal details from the
draft should be published without separate review.

Retain its useful distinctions:

- Person, creative work, project name and platform are different subjects.
- Copying, naming confusion, impersonation, unwanted disclosure and threats
  need different factual questions and response routes.
- Preserve sources and competing explanations before drawing conclusions.
- A proposed response needs a reason, scope, limitations and human decision.
- Private incident records should not be stored in a public code repository.

Do not adopt the draft's legal or technical conclusions wholesale:

| Draft proposition | Required specification correction |
| --- | --- |
| Headers and hashes prove authorship, ownership or a date | A digest compares bytes. Authorship, identity, trusted time and ownership require separate evidence. |
| Brief quotation with credit is fair use | Credit and brevity alone do not decide fair use; the Copyright Office describes a case-specific, multifactor inquiry. |
| Every modified redistribution must have a different name | Do not add a blanket restriction to Apache-licensed code. Section 6 withholds trademark permission; specific naming claims require separate review. |
| An inventory in another local mirror is this checkout's ground truth | Verify this repository and revision independently; the draft's repository URL and inventory are not current-checkout findings. |
| Public disclosure eliminates every possible trade-secret/access claim | Do not make categorical historical or jurisdictional conclusions. Separate public contents, previously confidential material, disclosure timing and alleged acquisition. |
| Preservation means never deleting private records | Preserve analytical correction lineage without imposing indefinite personal-data retention. Provide explicit retention, deletion and legal-hold review. |
| Filing is the default after a checklist passes | Checklist completion is not legal judgment or authority. Preparation, human review and external execution remain distinct. |
| Family membership supplies consent | Each person's data and permissions are separate. Relationship, payment or household administration is not blanket access authority. |

Other draft assertions about court cases, platform rules, registration,
compensation, remedies and enforceability remain UNVERIFIED unless independently
reviewed against applicable primary sources. No new NOTICE, trademark declaration,
social-media policy, license restriction or legal filing is adopted here.

## Candidate capabilities

| Capability | Proposed assistance | Explicit boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Privacy planning | User-selected data inventory, purpose, recipients, retention and disclosure review | No account scraping, background collection or automatic uploads |
| Account and identity safety | Review user-supplied alerts; prepare recovery and impersonation checklists | No passwords, recovery codes, impersonation accusations or automatic account changes |
| Scam and message assessment | Analyze voluntarily supplied messages, links and payment requests | No certainty from appearance; do not follow links or send payments automatically |
| Harassment and unwanted disclosure | Build a private, source-attributed incident timeline and possible reporting routes | No surveillance, retaliation, doxxing or automatic confrontation |
| Household device safety | Explain consented account/device settings and consequences | No covert tracking or automatic monitoring-software removal |
| Rights research | Show jurisdiction, source edition, elements, exceptions, enforcement actor and access limits | Legal information, not counsel, a verdict or complete national protection |
| Response preparation | Produce redacted drafts and review checklists for a chosen recipient | No complaint, takedown, notification, signature or filing without explicit authorization |
| Family coordination | Share selected records or tasks with a chosen person | No default household-wide view; no authority inferred from being a guardian |

Minor-specific features require separate research into age, capacity, applicable
law, guardian authority and the child's privacy and safety. Do not build a
child-monitoring feature by repurposing adult consent. Health, financial and
legal advice are not replaced by the agent.

## Safety and consent requirements

1. Ask whether the current device and communications channel are safe before
   suggesting sensitive activity. Do not assume a monitored device can be made
   safe through this application.
2. Do not automatically change passwords, remove software, disable sharing,
   confront someone or notify family. Such actions can alert another person,
   destroy evidence or increase danger.
3. Offer user-selected access to qualified support and emergency resources.
   The agent is not an emergency responder; recommendations must be appropriate
   to the supplied location and verified resource access.
4. Separate the affected person from a requester, helper, guardian, reviewer
   and execution approver. None of those roles implies the others.
5. Permissions must name person, purpose, record scope, recipient, expiry and
   revocation behavior. Refusal or revocation must not trigger family alerts.
6. New household membership must not expose older private records. Removal must
   stop future access; already exported copies cannot be recalled by a promise.
7. Sharing must preview exact fields, attachments and identifying metadata.
   Redaction is not automatically anonymization.
8. No hidden location tracking, keylogging, ambient recording, relationship
   scoring, political classification or speculative offender identification.

These are proposed requirements, not implemented controls.

## Data lifecycle and trust boundaries

```text
Voluntary, scoped intake
  -> minimum necessary private record
  -> source-access and provenance review
  -> bounded analysis with alternative explanations
  -> private preview and affected-person perspective
  -> separate human completion and release decision
  -> explicitly scoped sharing or execution approval
  -> confirmed outcome or explicit failure
  -> user-controlled retention and deletion review
```

For a future contract, distinguish:

- Case identity, affected-person identifiers, jurisdiction and safety context.
- Evidence facts, user reports, inferences and external-source access.
- Consent grants and revocations, independent of confidence and case status.
- Legal references: statute/policy/bill/court decision, source edition,
  inspected scope, applicability UNKNOWN and enforceability UNVERIFIED.
- Proposed action, recipient, exact payload preview, exposure risks, approval
  identity and expiry; execution receipt must report actual outcome.
- Private originals, redacted sharing copies and minimal audit events.

Do not embed private identifiers or case contents in public manifests, GitHub
issues, telemetry or static Pages assets. Do not promise "local-only" while
runtime dependencies, external models or other services make network requests.
Research queries must omit private incident details unless specifically approved.

Retention must include purpose and expiry, export, access revocation, deletion
of raw data and derived copies, backups and embeddings if introduced. A minimal
deletion audit must not preserve the deleted private text. Legal holds and
conflicting requests require explicit review, not indefinite silent retention.
Keep historical source artifacts intact; private-data deletion requirements
must be designed separately from immutable analytical correction lineage.

## Relationship to the current implementation

The current architecture explicitly excludes multiuser/tenant isolation.
Its single-owner review credentials and SQLite workflows are not evidence of
safe family isolation. Do not expose them to multiple family members as-is.

The existing specialist API, evidence methods, preview/release separation and
human control plane are candidates for reuse after contract review. The static
GitHub Pages verifier is not a private family case workspace. Preserve existing
entry points and validated methods while designing the new service.

Deployment, account model, custody, encryption/key recovery, offline operation,
family sharing and external model providers are NOT_SELECTED. No implementation
or migration should infer those decisions.

## Proposed contract handoffs

This table is a requirements map, not a new JSON schema or API. New fields and
routes require reviewed implementation and compatibility tests before use.

| Boundary | Required information or decision | Current/proposed distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Private intake | Affected person, safe channel, purpose, authority, data minimization and retention | Proposed; no household identity or consent API |
| Evidence task | Bounded question, source descriptions, lineage and optional inquiry/model context | Existing [specialist contract](specialist-agent.md); caller labels remain assertions |
| Rights/process review | Jurisdiction, source edition/access, elements, exceptions, enforcement actor and missing facts | Proposed workflow using bounded legal references; no eligibility engine |
| Response draft | Specific requested remedy, recipient, redacted payload, risks and missing requirements | Proposed; guide templates are not submissions or sworn filings |
| Human completion/release | Exact evidence preview, inquiry revision and separate human report decision | Existing supporting lifecycle; not legal approval or sharing consent |
| External action | Explicit approver, exact recipient/payload/action, expiry and actual receipt | Not authorized by this proposal; existing GitHub study dispatch is a separate surface |
| Retention/deletion | Original/derivative/backup inventory, requested scope, conflicts and minimal deletion audit | Proposed private-data lifecycle; current pruning is not certified secure erasure |

### Distinct state vocabularies

- **Workflow lifecycle:** existing PENDING, RUNNING, AWAITING_APPROVAL,
  APPROVED, COMPLETED, REJECTED and FAILED concern evidence reports.
  COMPLETED does not mean a person is protected or an external action succeeded.
- **Source standing:** SOURCE-ESTABLISHED and UNVERIFIED describe inspected
  legal-source access in the catalogs, not legal enforceability.
- **Jurisdiction:** a US state name is a location/reference, not a lifecycle
  value, governing-law determination or uniform national right.
- **Permissions and action outcomes:** future consent, revocation, submission
  and remedy states must be independently defined and audited; do not overload
  report state, confidence or filing colors to represent them.

The protection guide remains pending owner editing. An edit may change proposed
requirements but cannot silently migrate permissions, modify source evidence,
adopt legal terms or authorize external action.

## Acceptance criteria before implementation release

- A second person cannot read, infer, export or mutate an unshared case through
  API, UI, search, caches, attachments or logs.
- Expired/revoked permissions fail closed; new members cannot inherit history.
- Declining sharing or help does not notify a potentially unsafe contact.
- Supplied allegations stay reports; unknown attribution stays unknown.
- Legal search failure stays UNVERIFIED; bills and outdated editions are not
  presented as current enforceable protections.
- No execution occurs from analysis, a checklist, family membership or release.
- Export previews match actual payloads; sensitive metadata is tested explicitly.
- Retention/deletion behavior is demonstrated across originals, derivatives,
  backups and any search index, not just a hidden UI row.
- Network behavior and third-party exposure are measured and disclosed.
- Coercive-control, compromised-device and unsafe-notification scenarios are
  tested without assuming that immediate technical remediation is safest.
- An independent access-boundary review and user acceptance against exact
  source/preview are required; passing unit tests is not a safety certification.

## Primary-source research record

This is a bounded first pass, not a fifty-state family-rights review. Source
access establishes only inspected text, not application to a person.

| ID | Source opened | Supported observation | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PF-01 | [NIST Privacy Framework: getting started](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework/getting-started-0) | Privacy risk includes harms from data operations throughout collection-to-disposal; cybersecurity alone is insufficient. | Voluntary guidance; excerpt truncated after framework structure. No certification or complete control mapping. |
| PF-02 | [FTC: Stalkerware, What To Know](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/stalkerware-what-know) | Removing monitoring software can alert an abusive person; safety planning, safer communications and evidence considerations precede changes. | Fetch returned 403; ordinary browser displayed substantive guidance. Not evidence any user's device is monitored. |
| PF-03 | [Copyright Office: Copyright in General](https://www.copyright.gov/help/faq/faq-general.html) | Copyright concerns fixed expression; ideas and systems differ; registration has separate procedural significance. | General guidance, not a repository ownership finding or registration search. |
| PF-04 | [Copyright Office: Fair Use Index](https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/) | Fair use is case-specific and multifactor; even quantity alone is not decisive. | Overview excerpt, not a court opinion or a verdict on any proposed use. |
| PF-05 | [Washington RCW 4.24.790](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=4.24.790) | Electronic impersonation provision includes consent, intent, injury, exclusions and limits on provider liability. | Statutory text opened; current case law and any particular person's elements not assessed. |
| PF-06 | [Repository Apache license](../LICENSE) | Sections 2, 4 and 6 separate copying permissions, redistribution conditions and trademark permissions. | Existing file inspected; no license amendment, trademark ownership or infringement finding. |

SEARCH RECORD: personal/family privacy-risk and draft-claim verification /
official web fetch, one targeted stalkerware discovery search, ordinary browser
and local draft/license reads / named sources above / six supporting sources
opened / limit hit yes: selected excerpts and scope / primary source opened yes
for listed observations / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for inspected guidance and text
only; product effectiveness UNVERIFIED / all-state rights, family authority,
child-specific law, court status, platform policies and deployment design NOT
checked exhaustively.

FTC business-data and COPPA pages returned 403 through fetch; child identity-theft
guidance was not substantively opened in that initial pass. Subsequent parallel
research opened FTC child-identity guidance and the rendered IdentityTheft.gov
homepage; see the companion [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md)
for source-attributed observations and limits. A 2023 COPPA snapshot does not
establish current requirements. CISA and Safety Net initial fetches exposed
navigation, title or incomplete content. They remain research leads,
not corroboration or support for new legal claims. NIST version 1.1 appeared as
an initial draft on the landing page; no final-version claim is made.

## Next research decisions

First select a narrow initial assistance area and deployment/access model.
Then deepen research into affected-person consent, minors/guardianship,
jurisdictional remedies, privacy threat models and safe response options for that
area. Expand the legal catalog without calling it complete protection.
Only after those decisions should a typed contract and implementation plan be
approved. No external filing, monitoring or account integration is authorized.
