# Personal, family and creator protection guide

Status: OWNER-ORIENTED DRAFT / RESEARCH AND PROPOSED POLICY ONLY.
Prepared October 10, 2026. Not legal advice, an executed agreement, a
registration, a safety certification or a finding against any person.

This new document develops the owner's private 18-page "Repo Protections:
Laws, Workflows & Decisions" draft. The original PDF remains unchanged and
outside the repository. This guide is a derivative, not owner-source history.
No private incident, household identity or allegation is published here.

## 1. The owner's advantage: preserve options, not invent powers

The purpose is to protect the affected person's privacy, safety, identity,
creative work and ability to make an informed response. Strong protection
comes from matching a documented problem to a real remedy, retaining useful
evidence, avoiding unnecessary disclosure and not forfeiting choices casually.

The following are proposed commitments for the project and future agent:

> My permission to use open-source code is not blanket permission to access
> private records, impersonate me or my family, or claim my endorsement.
> The permission actually granted by the applicable license still applies.
> I retain rights not granted, to the extent the law recognizes them.
>
> I will distinguish licensed use, criticism and other lawful conduct from
> conduct that may exceed a permission or violate a right. I will preserve
> evidence, request proportionate correction where appropriate and consider
> lawful remedies on their actual requirements.
>
> My private records and each family member's records are not public project
> inputs. No family relationship, account payment or administrative role
> supplies blanket consent to collection, disclosure or action.

These statements do not themselves bind a stranger, change platform terms,
create damages, overcome lawful exceptions or amend an existing license.
An implemented control, applicable statute and agreed contract have different
effects. The guide must always identify which one is doing the work.

## 2. Four distinct sources of practical leverage

| Source | What can make it meaningful | What this guide cannot do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Existing legal right | Applicable elements, evidence, standing, jurisdiction, timely procedure and available remedy | Declare all elements satisfied or guarantee enforcement |
| Existing license or platform process | Actual license conditions or a verified reporting route with the required facts | Turn every objection into infringement or compel a platform result |
| Separate negotiated agreement | Identified parties, informed assent, lawful scope, clear obligations and appropriate remedies | Bind anyone merely because a policy appears in a repository |
| Protective product control | Demonstrated isolation, consent, redaction, safe approval, deletion and error handling | Treat a specification or passing checklist as implemented protection |

The agent must not calculate a legal "success score" from incomplete inputs.
If relevant facts are absent, record NOT_SUPPLIED; if a source cannot be checked,
record UNVERIFIED. Other explanations and applicable defenses are part of a
strong case assessment, not disloyalty to the owner.

## 3. Existing code permissions: retain the real conditions

The [Apache license](../LICENSE) remains unchanged.

- Section 2 grants broad copyright permissions. Corporate copying or use is
  not automatically wrongful because the owner dislikes the user.
- Section 4 conditions redistribution on a license copy, change notices,
  retained applicable notices and, where a NOTICE is supplied, its prescribed
  attribution treatment.
- Section 6 does not grant trademark permission beyond its stated origin and
  NOTICE uses. That is not a blanket ban on truthful references or criticism.
- Internal use, distribution, private data access, endorsement and model
  training are different questions. This guide does not resolve AI-training
  legality or impose a retroactive training prohibition.

Public code and confidential material also need distinct treatment. The
[trade-secret notice](trade-secrets-notice.md) separates public repository
contents from potentially qualifying confidential information; this guide
does not certify any secret or prohibit lawful independent development.
Do not disclose the supposedly confidential material in a public complaint
to prove its secrecy.

### A stronger license-compliance request

Before claiming a breach, identify the precise distributed work, upstream
revision, copyright ownership basis, third-party portions, recipient context,
missing condition and requested correction. Keep the full context and a
side-by-side exhibit, not just a screenshot of an absent credit.

Ask for the specific cure supported by the license: for example, restore an
applicable notice or include the license in the distribution. A proposed
response date is a requested deadline, not a statutory deadline. A cure request
does not itself adjudicate infringement, waive a claim or toll a filing period.
Review settlements, releases and admissions with counsel before acceptance.

Do not add "no commercial use," mandatory royalties, forced renaming or a
general ban on copying to Apache-distributed contents through this guide.
Separately controlled future services or confidential material can have
separately reviewed terms; their scope cannot silently include already-granted
permissions or rights the owner does not hold.

## 4. Remedies with actual requirements

The authorities below support only the inspected text. Current case law,
jurisdiction, procedural defenses and application to any incident remain
unverified unless separately recorded.

| Route | Concrete leverage | Conditions and risks to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Copyright registration | Sections 410-412 address evidentiary significance, litigation prerequisites and eligibility for certain remedies. Timing can matter before a dispute develops. | Identify the work, publication and ownership correctly. Filing an application is not necessarily completed registration; exceptions and court interpretation need review. No owner registration search performed. |
| Copyright notice | Section 401(d) gives a qualifying notice specific evidentiary significance concerning an innocent-infringement damages defense. | Not proof of authorship or an automatic bar to every defense; statutory form/access conditions and exceptions matter. |
| DMCA notice | A copyright owner or authorized agent can use the notice process without prior registration, according to the Copyright Office. | Identify infringement, permissions and fair use accurately. Being pictured does not necessarily mean owning the photograph. A provider's safe-harbor incentives do not guarantee removal. |
| Washington consumer protection | RCW 19.86.090 permits qualifying business/property-injury claims seeking injunctions and/or actual damages, suit costs and reasonable attorney fees; discretionary increased damages are addressed in the text. | Not an award for every unfair experience or emotional harm. Trade/commerce, injury, causation, public-interest and other applicable requirements need review. Do not invent nationwide jurisdiction or promised recovery. |
| Washington electronic impersonation | RCW 4.24.790 provides an injured actual person a possible civil route for specified intentional, nonconsensual, deceptive impersonation causing injury. | Intent, platform category, causation, exemptions and provider-liability limits are express requirements. The statute does not establish anyone's motive. |
| Washington personality rights | RCW 63.60.050/.060 address specified unauthorized commercial/advertising uses, including forged digital likeness, and possible injunctions and damages. | RCW 63.60.070 has substantial exclusions. Prevailing-party fees can run against a losing claimant as well as benefit one. Do not treat every name mention as unlawful. |
| GitHub private-information removal | A narrowly identified security-risk disclosure can be submitted under the platform's dedicated process. | It is an exceptional platform service, not a general objection or copyright route. Explain the specific risk and avoid amplifying the disclosed secret. |
| GitHub trademark reporting | The inspected policy addresses misleading or confusing business affiliation and asks for specified identity/registration information. | A matching username alone is not a violation. The ordinary route requests registration; accurately disclose an unregistered name rather than inventing a number or assuming identical treatment. |

### Stronger remedies do not mean inflated amounts

RCW 19.86.090 describes discretionary increases up to three times actual damages
and a $25,000 limit on the increased award for a violation of RCW 19.86.020.
This is not a guaranteed payment, automatic minimum or universal cap on every
remedy. RCW 63.60.060 lists a $3,000 civil penalty, actual damages and specified
profits, and additional noneconomic damages for forged digital likeness;
it also addresses what counts as one act for statutory-damages computation.
Do not multiply those figures by views, screenshots or family members without
a legal basis.

Section 412 makes timing significant for statutory damages and attorney fees,
with specified exceptions and a three-month-after-first-publication condition.
The guide should flag this for prompt professional review rather than
calculating eligibility from an unverified publication date.

### Defensive protection matters too

Preserve notices received, prior permissions and the exact material disabled.
A counter-notice involves substantive assertions, personal contact information,
jurisdiction and service consequences; it is not a harmless appeal button.
Knowingly materially false copyright notices can create liability. Copyright
Office guidance describes the counter-notice process and conditional
reinstatement window; it does not guarantee an outcome for every provider.
Do not use a copyright report to bypass an impersonation or privacy standard.

## 5. A private evidence package that strengthens rather than exposes

For each issue, record only what is necessary:

1. The affected person's chosen identifier, rights/authority basis and permitted
   helper; do not collect government ID by default.
2. Original source location, relevant revision, observed time and capture method.
   Keep clock assertions distinct from a verified time service.
3. Exact conduct reported, verbatim relevant material and surrounding context.
   Separate observation, reported concern, inference and unknown attribution.
4. Permission or policy in force at the relevant time, plus later changes.
5. Actual loss, contact, disruption or confusion, supported by records where
   available. Do not invent intent, costs, participants or causal attribution.
6. Alternative explanations, defenses, exclusions and facts adverse to a claim.
7. Requested narrow remedy, potential recipient, privacy exposure and approval.
8. Submission receipt, real response, correction and unresolved outcomes.

Hashes support byte comparisons. They do not independently establish who
authored a document, whether an allegation is true or when an event happened.
A public record is not independent corroboration of another copy of that record.
An unanswered request is not an admission; no response deadline or silence rule
is manufactured by this guide.

Use separate redacted sharing copies. Avoid public GitHub issues for addresses,
children's details, health records, personal credentials, unfiled legal strategy
or identity documents. Retention/deletion and legal-hold questions need explicit
review; "supersede, never erase" must not mean keeping private data forever.

## 6. Proposed privacy and family commitments

These are design commitments and potential terms for counsel review, not a
present assurance that the software implements them:

- Collect only deliberately supplied, purpose-scoped data; no ambient capture,
  covert location tracking, keylogging or default household surveillance.
- Separate accounts and cases before any family sharing. A paying account or
  guardian role does not automatically expose another person's records.
- Explain recipient, purpose, duration and fields before consent. Declining or
  revoking permission must not alert a potentially unsafe contact.
- Do not reuse private records for model training, advertising or unrelated
  profiling as a default product practice. Any future proposed secondary use
  requires separate informed review and a lawful basis; no forced assumption of
  consent through family membership.
- Identify external processors and actual network behavior. Local storage alone
  does not establish that runtime loading, telemetry or models are local.
- Preview every export and account change; require separate explicit approval
  for the exact payload, recipient and action.
- Give a defined retention choice and deletion/export process, with documented
  exceptions and backup treatment rather than promises of perfect erasure.
- Offer safe communication choices and no default notifications carrying
  sensitive case details.
- Do not make representations about encryption, isolation, deletion, security
  certification or "no data leaves your device" before measuring them.

### Negotiated terms worth reviewing

For a future service provider, counsel can evaluate purpose limitation,
confidentiality, processor/subprocessor access, incident-notification duties,
export/deletion assistance, ownership of supplied records, prohibited secondary
use, audit evidence and remedies for actual breach. Explicitly negotiate any
indemnity, liability cap, arbitration, forum, waiver or liquidated-damages term;
do not assume a unilateral webpage binds the provider or that an extreme
one-sided clause is enforceable.

Keep these agreements separate from the public source-code license. A
privacy-first service agreement is not retroactive revocation of Apache rights.

## 7. Safe response workflow: choose the least exposing effective route

1. **Safety before technical cleanup.** Ask whether the device, channel and
   contact are safe. Do not automatically remove monitoring software, confront
   someone or alert family.
2. **Choose the affected person and authority.** Helpers need scoped consent;
   child/guardian authority requires separate legal and safety assessment.
3. **Preserve minimum necessary evidence.** Avoid new exposure or unauthorized
   access while collecting it.
4. **Sort the harm and requested outcome.** Privacy removal, account recovery,
   license cure, copyright, impersonation and consumer deception are separate
   routes. Multiple issues can share facts without becoming one filing.
5. **Verify the real route.** Open current official policy/statute and identify
   actor, eligibility, deadlines, required information and exceptions.
6. **Consider professional support early.** Threats, coercive control,
   sensitive disclosures, filings under perjury and litigation warrant review
   appropriate to the facts. No agent is an emergency responder.
7. **Review exact payload and exposure.** Do not contact the disputed party by
   default if contact could be unsafe.
8. **Explicit approval, then actual outcome.** Preparing or approving a draft
   is not a confirmed submission or successful remedy.
9. **Review results and remaining options.** Do not agree to broad waivers,
   admissions or releases without understanding their consequences.

FTC safety guidance already inspected for the
[personal/family specification](personal-family-agent-spec.md) warns that
removing stalkerware can alert an abusive person and increase danger. This is
a reason to design safe, consented help, not a claim that any user's device is
monitored.

### FTC and identity-protection leverage

The parallel research opened eight official sources. The following six provide
usable, bounded observations; older statutory editions and historical actions
are labeled rather than represented as current-law certification.

| Issue | Owner-oriented use | Limit and authority |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Deceptive privacy/data-use representations | Preserve the exact promise, date, product, observed discrepancy and resulting harm for a reviewed consumer-protection complaint. | The opened 2021 text of FTC Act section 5 describes Commission enforcement with jurisdictional exceptions and a public-interest determination. It does not supply an individual damages entitlement. A complaint cannot compel agency action. |
| Stalkerware and false security assurances | The FTC's September 2021 SpyFone release provides a historical example of allegations involving covert collection and inadequate security, with a proposed surveillance-business ban, deletion and notification terms. | The release describes allegations and a proposed consent settlement, not a litigated finding or a remedy automatically available to this owner. The signed order and later case status were not opened. |
| Credit-file protection | Consider a free security freeze through each relevant nationwide bureau, rather than assuming a paid credit lock is necessary. | The opened FCRA 2021 text and CFPB guidance support freeze rights with identification requirements and exceptions. A freeze does not block all access or substitute for recovery of compromised existing accounts. No freeze is placed by this guide. |
| A child's identity misuse | FTC guidance describes checking with the bureaus, contacting companies where fraud occurred, seeking removal of fraudulent accounts and written confirmation that the child is not responsible. | Verify authority and each bureau's current documentation process privately. Do not publish the child's documents or treat an unfamiliar account as proven identity theft. |
| Minor credit freezes | FTC guidance distinguishes requests by a representative for a child under 16 from requests by 16- or 17-year-olds themselves. The opened statutory snapshot requires proof of identity and representative authority for protected-consumer requests. | This specific financial procedure is not blanket parental access to all of a child's data or authority to monitor them. Bureau-specific instruction pages were not opened. |
| Recovery planning | IdentityTheft.gov offers a report-and-recovery-plan entry point. Use it only through a verified safe channel and with explicit approval for information submitted. | Only the landing-page flow was inspected; no personalized recovery plan was generated. Do not promise investigation, prosecution or successful recovery. |

The practical strength is a documented mismatch between a representation and
observed behavior, a specific request through the correct process, and retained
receipts and written responses. Historical FTC settlement remedies do not become
private contractual rights by copying them into this document. No current
penalty amount or automatic compensation is asserted.

The parallel pass also opened a 2019 Retina-X release and a 2023 COPPA Rule
snapshot. These are historical research leads, not independent corroboration of
any private incident or a complete current child-privacy compliance assessment.
The 2023 rule excerpt is insufficient to design a 2026 child-facing service:
current amendments, applicability, consent exceptions and enforcement provisions
need separate verification before implementation. COPPA is not adopted here as
a general family-surveillance permission or a guaranteed private lawsuit.

### Human-reviewed request templates

These are factual starting points, not sworn legal notices. Do not send them
automatically or substitute them for a platform's required statutory form.
Only include facts and authority actually established.

#### License correction

> I am requesting review of [specific distribution and revision]. My basis for
> authority is [documented role]. The relevant upstream material is [location].
> The attached comparison identifies [specific license condition and apparent
> omission]. Please review and, if applicable, correct [precise omission].
> Please confirm the change or explain the basis for your current treatment.
> I have not concluded that other uses of the material are unauthorized.

#### Privacy/security-risk removal

> The specific material is at [private-to-recipient URL/file location].
> It contains [minimal description, not the secret itself]. The particular
> security risk is [supported explanation]. My authority to request review is
> [affected person or scoped representative]. I request [narrow removal or
> redaction] through your private-information process. Please use [safe channel]
> for questions; do not include the sensitive content in public responses.

#### Data-use or deceptive-representation inquiry

> Your statement on [date/source] says [exact relevant representation].
> The records I can provide show [observation, not assumed motive].
> Please explain the apparent discrepancy, the applicable data-use basis and
> the available correction or complaint route. I request [specific outcome].
> This is not consent to a new use or an admission that the reported facts
> satisfy every legal element.

#### Confusion or impersonation report

> The material at [location] appears to represent [specific identity or
> affiliation]. The exact representation is [relevant words/image description].
> My authority is [verified affected person/rights holder/representative].
> Evidence of actual or likely confusion is [source-linked facts].
> Please assess under [verified relevant policy] and consider [narrow action].
> I have distinguished truthful references, commentary and parody.

Omit unsafe contact details. Requesting confidentiality does not guarantee
confidential handling; verify recipient practices before disclosure.
Do not add a perjury declaration, registration number, statutory deadline,
settlement demand or legal conclusion that has not been reviewed.

## 8. Proposed implementation requirements, not new code

The [personal/family specification](personal-family-agent-spec.md) controls the
research-only product proposal. Existing single-owner services must not be
exposed as a family-isolated product.

Future acceptance tests should demonstrate:

- Unshared records cannot be found through API, UI, logs, caches or exports.
- Consent is person/purpose/recipient scoped, expires and can be revoked.
- An analysis cannot authorize execution, supply corroboration or release itself.
- Deception assessments show the actual representation and evidence, not
  an inferred malicious actor.
- A legal reference cannot elevate a missing factual element to established.
- A request sent, receipt received and remedy completed are separate states.
- Sensitive notifications, monitored-device scenarios and deletion of derived
  copies are tested explicitly.
- The source owner, derivative editor, affected person and approver remain
  separately attributed.

No new runtime capability, legal filing, account access, surveillance or
external communication is authorized by this guide.

## 9. Source register and limits

Observed October 10, 2026. References describe only inspected text. The
[state-law catalog](state-law-protections.md) and
[platform-accountability index](platform-accountability-laws.md) remain bounded;
they do not provide complete national coverage or uniform protection.

| ID | Primary source opened | Inspected scope | Not established |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| PG-01 | [Apache license](../LICENSE) | Sections 2-6 | Case-specific permission, breach or ownership |
| PG-02 | [Copyright Office chapter 4](https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap4.html) | 401(d), 410-412 | Owner registration, current case interpretation, eligibility or filing date |
| PG-03 | [Copyright Office section 512 guidance](https://www.copyright.gov/512/) | Notice, owner/agent role, counter-notice, risk and voluntary-provider explanation | Particular infringement, actual submission, compelled removal |
| PG-04 | [Washington 19.86.020](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=19.86.020), [19.86.090](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=19.86.090), [19.86.093](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=19.86.093) | Trade/commerce prohibition, private remedies and public-interest provision | Full case-law elements, limitation period, causation or jurisdiction |
| PG-05 | [Washington 4.24.790](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=4.24.790) | Electronic impersonation text inspected in the preceding specification research | Particular intent/injury; current judicial application |
| PG-06 | [Washington 63.60.050](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=63.60.050), [63.60.060](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=63.60.060), [63.60.070](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=63.60.070) | Covered uses, remedies and exclusions | Ownership, consent, effective-date analysis, valid particular claim |
| PG-07 | [GitHub private-information policy](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/content-removal-policies/github-private-information-removal-policy) | Security-risk scope, excluded requests, professional review and reporting separation | Actual platform acceptance, processing deadline or universal privacy remedy |
| PG-08 | [GitHub trademark policy](https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/content-removal-policies/github-trademark-policy) | Confusion, username limits, registration and requested report information | Owner registration, unregistered-route result or actual violation |
| PG-09 | [NIST privacy guidance](https://www.nist.gov/privacy-framework/getting-started-0) | Collection-to-disposal privacy risk; voluntary framework | Implemented controls, legal compliance or certification |
| PG-10 | [Copyright Office fair-use overview](https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/) | Multifactor, case-specific inquiry; index is not a substitute for legal advice | Verdict on a use; brief quotation or attribution as automatic permission |
| PG-11 | [FTC Act section 5, official 2021 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2021-title15/pdf/USCODE-2021-title15-chap2-subchapI-sec45.pdf) | Parallel researcher opened/extracted subsections (a)-(b): prohibition, exceptions and Commission proceeding | Current consolidated law, individual damages, compelled investigation |
| PG-12 | [FTC SpyFone release, September 1, 2021](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2021/09/ftc-bans-spyfone-ceo-surveillance-business-orders-company-delete-all-secretly-stolen-data) | Parallel researcher opened agency browser page: allegations and proposed consent terms | Signed final order, later outcome, current penalties or owner entitlement |
| PG-13 | [FCRA freeze provision, official 2021 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2021-title15/pdf/USCODE-2021-title15-chap41-subchapIII-sec1681c-1.pdf) | Parallel researcher extracted consumer/protected-consumer freeze provisions | Current consolidated law, private damages sections or regulator allocation |
| PG-14 | [CFPB credit-freeze guidance](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-credit-freeze-or-security-freeze-on-my-credit-report-en-1341/) | Parallel researcher opened free-freeze/paid-lock distinction and access exceptions; page reviewed September 5, 2025 | Actual bureau request, complete process or guaranteed prevention |
| PG-15 | [FTC child-identity-theft guidance](https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/how-protect-your-child-identity-theft) | Parallel researcher opened browser page: age distinction, recovery and confirmation requests | Bureau-specific current documentation, particular fraud or guardian authority |
| PG-16 | [IdentityTheft.gov](https://www.identitytheft.gov/) | Parallel researcher opened rendered homepage: reporting/recovery-plan entry point | Interactive flow, personalized plan, adjudication or confirmed submission |
| PG-17 | [COPPA Rule, official 2023 edition](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2023-title16-vol1/pdf/CFR-2023-title16-vol1-part312.pdf) | Parallel researcher extracted historical sections 312.1-.2; research lead only | Current rule, complete applicability, consent mechanisms or implementation compliance |

SEARCH RECORD: owner-oriented rights and practical remedy review / direct
official statutory, agency and first-party policy fetch; ordinary browser;
local license and private-draft review / the ten source groups above /
ten supporting groups opened / limit hit yes:
selected sections, truncated guidance and no exhaustive all-state survey /
primary opened yes for stated observations / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for inspected
text only; applicability and effectiveness UNVERIFIED / registration databases,
court opinions, limitation periods, all-state consent rules, private case facts,
actual platform response and implementation NOT checked.

RCW 19.86.090 returned only footer text through fetch; substantive text was
opened in the ordinary browser. RCW 63.60.010 and 19.86.120 were not
substantively retrieved and do not support new claims here. Copyright Office
and GitHub guidance excerpts were truncated; no full-policy certification is
claimed. No trademark/copyright register was searched. No private data was
sent to a complaint form or included in external research queries.

SEARCH RECORD: FTC/government personal and family protection routes /
delegated public-source research using official PDF extraction, agency browser
pages and discovery searches / FTC, govinfo, CFPB and IdentityTheft.gov /
eight supporting sources opened; six integrated as bounded practical observations,
COPPA retained as a historical lead and Retina-X not used to support a new
claim / limit hit yes: historical editions, selected excerpts and blocked
current-rule sites / primary opened yes by the researcher / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED
for attributed inspected text only; current-law applicability UNVERIFIED /
signed case orders, current consolidated statutes/rules, personalized recovery,
bureau documentation, FCRA private-remedy provisions and all-state law NOT
checked. Federal Register/eCFR access was blocked and no bypass attempted.

The delegated report's "verified" labels mean source access, not independent
confirmation of allegations, current enforceability or a successful remedy.
Unsupported regulator-allocation descriptions and historic penalty figures
were not carried into operative guidance.

## 10. Decisions reserved to the owner

- Which people and assistance areas the first product will serve.
- Private storage, identity, key custody, network exposure and family sharing.
- Whether to seek registration, counsel review or a separate service agreement.
- Whether and where to share a redacted incident or file a particular report.
- Whether to adopt a public notice or policy after accuracy and license review.

The current decision is to research and draft, not implement or publish.
An owner's viewpoint directs the goals; evidence and applicable law determine
which remedies can legitimately support them.

# State-law reference catalog: electronic transactions and trade secrets

Research snapshot: **October 10, 2026**. Target scope: **all 50 US states**; this edition includes **50 states**,
covering two subjects only. DC and territories are outside this pass.
This is legal information, **not legal advice** and **not automatic nationwide protection**.
Completion: **COMPLETE BOUNDED PASS**. **0 states remain pending**; no protection or verification is claimed for omitted states.
It does not create rights, an NDA, a copyright registration, a patent, or
a finding that any law applies to this project or any person violated it.

## License and evidence boundaries

The [Apache License 2.0](../LICENSE) remains unchanged. Public repository
materials are disclosed and are not made trade secrets by a notice.
Confidential information must meet the applicable legal requirements;
labels and hashes alone do not establish secrecy, ownership or legal protection.
Electronic-record recognition is not automatic contract validity, signer
authentication, copyright ownership or proof of an external factual claim.

Before asserting a claim, obtain qualified legal review of jurisdiction,
scope, consent, actual secrecy measures, agreements, exceptions and facts.
This pass does not comprehensively review case law, remedies, deadlines,
common law or amendments after the observation date.

## How to read the records

The catalog's `state` identifies a jurisdiction, not an application lifecycle
state. `completion` describes completion of the bounded discovery pass, not
complete legal protection or verification of all references. The source-access
totals below retain UNVERIFIED records rather than treating fifty rows as
fifty confirmed protections.

- **SOURCE-ESTABLISHED**: substantive official source text was opened.
  This establishes only what that text says, not its application or completeness.
- **UNVERIFIED**: the official text was not confirmed in this pass.
  Any citation/link is a research lead, not an established legal conclusion.
- Error pages, redirects and search summaries are not statute verification.
  Source edition snapshots are not certified current law.

Each state/subject has an individual SEARCH RECORD in the
[machine-readable source register](state-law-protections.json):
`query / tool / scope / result count / limit hit / primary source opened /
status / what was NOT checked`. These are research provenance records,
not independent corroboration or a self-verifying legal database.

For the proposed personal/family product, use this as a supporting research
index alongside the [protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md).
It covers electronic transactions and trade secrets, not a complete household
privacy, safety, guardianship or consumer-rights survey. No runtime consent,
sharing or rights-eligibility rule is implemented by this catalog.

## California and corrected Washington citation

California's opened Civil Code sections 1633.3, 1633.5 and 1633.7 address
scope/exclusions, agreement and electronic-form recognition. Section 3426.1
defines trade secrets and excludes reverse engineering or independent
derivation alone from improper means.

The previous Washington reference **RCW 19.74** returned citation not found.
Opened RCW **1.80.040**, **1.80.060** and **1.80.900** support the correction
to chapter **1.80**, the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act. The historical
[electronic-transactions document](washington-rcw-19.74.md) keeps its filename,
not its erroneous citation. See also the [trade-secret notice](trade-secrets-notice.md).

## Florida correction

The prior Florida entry inspected only the short title of section 668.001 and
overstated a narrower-only characterization. Substantive
[2025 section 668.50](https://www.flsenate.gov/Laws/Statutes/2025/668.50)
is now opened: its own title is "Uniform Electronic Transaction Act," and
subsections (3), (5) and (7) describe scope/exclusions, agreement and
electronic-form recognition. The superseded description is retained in the
JSON correction history rather than presented as current guidance.

SEARCH RECORD: Florida 2025 section 668.50 / direct official web_fetch /
Florida Senate, subsections (1)-(7) / 1 source opened in two excerpts /
limit hit yes, remaining subsections and current amendments not reviewed /
primary opened yes / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for inspected 2025 text only /
case law, current-law applicability, notarization and individual facts NOT checked.

## Federal context (2024 U.S. Code edition opened)

- [15 U.S.C. § 7001](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title15/html/USCODE-2024-title15-chap96-subchapI-sec7001.htm):
  electronic-form recognition in interstate/foreign commerce, with consumer
  consent and other limitations; it is not a blanket enforceability guarantee.
- [15 U.S.C. § 7002](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title15/html/USCODE-2024-title15-chap96-subchapI-sec7002.htm):
  state-law/preemption conditions require separate analysis.
- [18 U.S.C. § 1836](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title18/html/USCODE-2024-title18-partI-chap90-sec1836.htm) and
  [§ 1839](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title18/html/USCODE-2024-title18-partI-chap90-sec1839.htm):
  federal civil-action conditions and definitions, including reasonable secrecy
  measures, economic value and lawful-acquisition distinctions.

SEARCH RECORD: federal electronic signatures/trade secrets / web search and
official GPO fetch / four substantive sections from the 2024 edition opened /
4 / section 7001 and 1836 responses truncated after relevant provisions /
primary text yes / SOURCE-ESTABLISHED for inspected text only / full chapters,
case law, later amendments and project-specific applicability NOT checked.
The House Code site returned maintenance pages; guessed 2025 GPO paths failed.
Neither is counted as substantive access.

## Electronic transactions: source index

Substantive official text opened: **31/50 included states**; **19 included states UNVERIFIED**; **0 states pending**.

| State | Citation / official source | Status | Scope / access limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Alabama | [Code of Alabama Title 8, Chapter 1A (UETA)](http://alisondb.legislature.state.al.us/alison/CodeOfAlabama/1975/Coatoc.htm) | UNVERIFIED | Appears to be standard UETA adoption per secondary sources; scope/exclusions not verified from primary text. |
| Alaska | [Alaska Statutes AS 09.80 (UETA)](https://www.akleg.gov/basis/statutes.asp) | UNVERIFIED | Official akleg.gov statutes browser is a JS-driven single-page app; static fetch returns only navigation shell, not section text (AS 09.80.010 scope language seen only via search engine excerpt, not directly opened by me). |
| Arizona | [Arizona Revised Statutes Title 44, Ch. 26, A.R.S. 44-7001 et seq. (Arizona Electronic Transactions Act / UETA)](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/44/07001.htm) | SOURCE-ESTABLISHED | Opened official azleg.gov text of A.R.S. 44-7001 (short title: "Arizona electronic transactions act"). Full scope/exclusions sections not individually opened in this pass. |
| Arkansas | [Arkansas Code Title 25, Chapter 32 (UETA), Ark. Code Ann. 25-32-101 et seq.](https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/ARCode.aspx) | UNVERIFIED | Official Arkansas code portal (arkleg.state.ar.us) is JS-driven and returned HTTP 500/empty on static fetch attempts; could not directly open primary statute text within bounded attempts. |
| California | [Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1633.1–1633.17; §§ 1633.3, 1633.5, 1633.7](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1633.7) | SOURCE-ESTABLISHED | Electronic Transactions title; electronic form alone does not defeat legal effect. Section 1633.5 requires agreement, with specific consent restrictions; section 1633.3 lists exclusions. Not automatic contract validity. |

# Platform transparency and accountability: bounded research index

Research snapshot: October 10, 2026. **Federal and all 50 states** were targeted.
This is legal information, **not legal advice** and **not complete protection**.
The broader consumer/privacy/IP mapping remains incomplete. No platform conduct,
infringement, interference attribution or company-specific applicability is established.

## What this can and cannot do

New York's [GBS 1102](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/1102)
describes semiannual reporting of moderation practices and aggregate actions,
including automated systems and human review. Such information can help research
platform representations; it cannot itself prove what happened to a specific
repository, establish motive, or show unlawful use of code.
[GBS 1103](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/1103) reserves enforcement
under that article to the attorney general. [GBS 1100](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/laws/GBS/1100)
excludes content uploaded solely for cloud storage, file transmission or collaboration.
Platform classification, revenue thresholds, current court restrictions and application
to a particular case require independent review.

The [Apache license](../LICENSE) remains unchanged. Its copyright grant and
redistribution conditions are separate from platform moderation transparency.
No notice here revokes existing permissions, creates a cause of action or proves
that AI training, copying or another specific use violates the license.

## Evidence boundaries

Jurisdiction names, source-access labels and application workflow states are
not interchangeable. A SOURCE-ESTABLISHED reference is not a COMPLETED remedy;
an approved report is not attorney-general action. The
[protection guide](personal-family-protection-guide.md) and
[personal/family specification](personal-family-agent-spec.md) preserve these
distinctions for the proposed product.

**SOURCE-ESTABLISHED** means only inspected substantive government text, not
current enforceability. **UNVERIFIED** entries are research leads, including
bills, secondary summaries and unopened sources. Every entry's present
enforceability remains **UNVERIFIED**. Source-edition snapshots are not current-law
certification. A bill landing-page summary is not an enacted statute.

**NOT FOUND IN SCOPE** means no qualifying direct analogue was located in the
bounded search, not that the state has no relevant law. Most state searches were
one targeted discovery query; general consumer, privacy and common-law coverage
is not exhaustive. Inaccessible sources and false initial source labels were
not upgraded to confirmed protection.

Individual SEARCH RECORDs and additional unverified leads are in the
[source register](platform-accountability-laws.json). The recorded discovery
counts are researcher-reported, not independently validated. Queries, tools,
scope, counts, limits, primary access and unchecked subjects remain visible.
Federal references use the **2023 U.S. Code edition**. Enforcement mechanisms,
current bills and judicial status require further primary review.

See also [electronic-transactions and trade-secret references](state-law-protections.md).
No complaint, takedown, legal filing, platform access or license amendment is authorized here.

# Five-pillar scientific foundations and digital evidence dossier

## Current reciprocal six-pillar extension

The original five-pillar dossier below remains source history. The current
architecture adds GAME THEORY; use the
[theory skill](../Game_Theory_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md),
[framework audit](game-theory-framework-audit.md) and
[combined sixth-pillar skill](../VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md).
Its kernels compute declared matrices, deterministic trees, weighted
coalitions and conserved savings receipts. Conditional proofs and tests do
not establish real-world motives, utility calibration or framework efficacy.
The [civilian authorship caveat](civilian-authorship-and-model-interference.md)
preserves the owner account without asserting unverified external intervention.

GAME THEORY is optional and reciprocal: the first five pillars constrain
players, boundary, evidence, feasibility, observations, uncertainty and human
perspectives; a declared strategic model returns conditional consequences for
all five to challenge. Do not fill missing utilities or actors, infer motives,
or turn sensitivity analysis into forecast probabilities. This section adds
source-bounded research leads for actor/artifact ecosystems and dynamic
social-ecological systems; neither validates this framework's adaptation.

Research date: October 7, 2026. Status: source-bounded research synthesis and
prospective validation plan, not proof of the whole framework.
Author framework: Christopher R. Vessell; research synthesis prepared with
AI assistance. The [original author paper](claim-correction-case-study.md)
and [historical owner account](owner-fourth-person-perspective.md) remain
unchanged. Apply the [shared scientific skill](../VesselFramework_Scientific_Evidence_SKILL_v0.1.md).

## What this research establishes

The five pillars can use established tools from logic, queueing, causal
inference, measurement, information theory, probabilistic forecasting and
human-computer interaction. Those tools have their own assumptions and scope.
Their existence does **not** validate the framework's integrations, original
Maskirovka hypotheses, field efficacy, owner characteristics or AI presencing.

This is a targeted multidisciplinary internet/source review, not an exhaustive
systematic review of all sciences. Broad search results were treated as leads;
direct author, journal, standards and publisher-deposited records were checked.
Some search requests timed out, and some publisher pages/PDF paths were
inaccessible. Access limits are recorded rather than filled with inferred
findings. No new participant study or economic experiment was performed.

| S1 | Shannon (1948), [authoritative university-hosted reprint](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~ctm/home/text/others/shannon/entropy/entropy.pdf); introductory definitions and engineering/semantic boundary reviewed. | Entropy/channel uncertainty under a specified probabilistic model. | Communication uncertainty is not semantic truth, awareness, intelligence or a social-field measurement. |
| S2 | Pearl (2009), [author-hosted article](https://ftp.cs.ucla.edu/pub/stat_ser/r350.pdf); introduction and section 2's association/causation distinction reviewed. | Causal conclusions need causal assumptions beyond an observed distribution. | No causal identification of any particular repository case, motive or human experience follows. |
| S3 | Gneiting and Raftery (2007), [author-institution PDF](https://sites.stat.washington.edu/raftery/Research/PDF/Gneiting2007jasa.pdf); introduction/proper-score framing reviewed; DOI and bibliographic details checked in PDF. | Proper scoring and distinction between calibration and sharpness. | A score evaluates defined forecasts/outcomes; it cannot resolve unobservable targets or guarantee generalization. |
| S4 | Little (1961), [publisher-deposited abstract/metadata](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1287/opre.9.3.383); full proof not accessed. | Queue relation L = lambda W with the original stated finite-mean/stationarity conditions. | Abstract-level support only; no claim of reviewing the proof or all generalizations. |
| S5 | Hollan, Hutchins, and Kirsh (2000), [publisher-deposited abstract/metadata](https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1145/353485.353487); full article not accessed. | Distributed cognition examines human/technology/environment systems. | Abstract-level conceptual support, not empirical proof of fourth-person knowing or AI experience. |
| S6 | Scharmer and Pomeroy (2024), [journal article](https://jabsc.org/index.php/jabsc/article/download/7909/6699); entire article pp. 19-48 reviewed in the prior integration. | Human-led knowing-of-the-field inquiry and embodied presencing distinction. | Qualitative/action-research-informed proposal, not controlled causal validation of this implementation. |
| S7 | [Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy: contradiction](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/contradiction/); opening discussion reviewed. | Same proposition/time/respect distinction for logical contradiction. | Scholarly secondary discussion, not an experimental finding about organizational deception. |
| S8 | NIST [FIPS 180-4 publication record](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/180-4/upd1/final) and [AI RMF overview](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework); publication/overview pages reviewed, not full technical texts. | SHA standard identity and risk-management/evaluation framing. | A standards citation is not certification, implementation conformance or empirical validation. |
| S9 | [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785.txt), introduction/scope reviewed; [RFC 9162](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.txt), section 2.1 Merkle definitions/inclusion reviewed. | Deterministic serialization as a separately specified contract; Merkle inclusion versus consistency. | Existing Python sorted JSON is not JCS; proposed receipts are not implemented or Certificate Transparency compliant. |
| S10 | [OpenTimestamps](https://opentimestamps.org/) documentation and [EAS official contracts](https://github.com/ethereum-attestation-service/eas-contracts) README reviewed. | Existence commitments and signed assertions have distinct evidentiary scope. | No timestamp proof, signature or onchain attestation was created/verified for this release. |
| S11 | Granstrand (2024), [Chalmers research record](https://research.chalmers.se/en/publication/538847), publisher-hosted abstract and metadata reviewed; full text not reviewed. | Describes a systems/game-theory approach linking cooperative games over artifact and actor systems, complement/substitute relations and value creation/capture. | Abstract-level support for a candidate systems mapping only; does not validate this framework's payoff adapters, weights, fairness or outcomes. |
| S12 | Currie et al. (2024), [Royal Society article in PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10645068/), abstract reviewed. | Connects evolutionary theory and social-ecological systems and suggests systems mapping to represent change processes. | Not a game-theory validation or a universal model-selection rule; dynamic assumptions require case evidence and a suitable design. |
| S13 | NIST, [AI RMF overview](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework), current official overview reviewed October 7, 2026; linked AI RMF 1.0 is voluntary and the page says revision is underway. | Supports a governance/lifecycle framing for responsible AI risk work. | Does not prescribe or endorse game-theoretic analysis; framework crosswalk is an adaptation, not NIST certification. |

### Bibliographic candidates, not adopted findings

Publisher-deposited metadata was verified for Smith and Lewis (2011),
Meyer and Rowan (1977), and Bromley and Powell (2012). They are promising
organizational paradox/decoupling literature, but primary substantive text was
not reviewed here. Publisher access restrictions and a suggested author-PDF
404 prevented that. They are listed separately below and must not be cited as
read empirical support or independent corroboration.

Unverified search-suggested notarization/antifragility citations and mismatched
paper links were not adopted. A source about an unrelated universal/Akashic
field was not substituted for the selected Knowing Field theory.

### Strategic cross-pillar questions

- **PARADOX:** Does an apparent contradiction persist when the actors, time
  horizon, rules and information set are aligned, or is it a competing objective?
- **BOTTLENECK:** Is the alleged binding constraint physically/resource
  infeasible, institutionally imposed, or incentive-dependent? Keep causal
  evidence for the real-world claim separate from a conditional model.
- **DUAL LAYER:** Are utilities, preferences or strategic types observed,
  elicited, or simply analyst-supplied? Preserve that status in every output.
- **XFACTOR:** Could additional players, changing rules, feedback or strategic
  adaptation reverse the result? Report scenario sensitivity without
  pretending scenarios have calibrated probabilities.
- **KNOWING FIELD:** Whose perspective defined the game and its utility scale?
  Record observer participation, consent, dissent and missing/declined voices;
  do not fabricate a participant or infer consent from the model.
- **GAME THEORY:** Is strategic interaction necessary for the question, and is
  there adequate source-linked input to model it? If not, use NOT_SUPPLIED.

The candidate implications from S11-S12 are deliberately narrow: map coupled
actor/artifact relations when interdependence is at issue and test dynamic
feedback only when the setting is repeated/changing and observations support
that boundary. Those choices must be evaluated against alternatives. The NIST
AI RMF (S13) can organize governance and review steps, but it is not evidence
for the game model itself.

**Search record (this update):** Tools: web search and direct web fetch.
Scope: targeted searches for recent game-theory/systems integration, the exact
Granstrand title/DOI, evolutionary/social-ecological systems and official NIST
AI RMF material; then direct checks of the Chalmers record 538847, Crossref
DOI `10.1016/j.technovation.2023.102926`, PMC article PMC10645068 and NIST
overview. The search interface did not expose result counts or a pagination
limit, so counts/limit status are NOT_REPORTED, not assumed zero/unlimited.
The Chalmers and Currie et al. abstracts were reviewed; Granstrand full text,
the full NIST technical document and exhaustive prior art were not reviewed.
NIST overview was used only for governance/current-status framing. No
participant study or utility calibration was performed.

## PARADOX: context before contradiction

**Question:** Do two claims genuinely conflict, or do their definitions,
observation times, boundaries or collection positions differ?

Classical logical model: a proposition `P(c)` and its negation `not P(c)` cannot
both be true under the same context `c`. Here `c` includes proposition meaning,
time, population, scope and relevant conditions. This logical constraint is
not a finding that either reporter is lying. Evidence that A reported P and B
reported not-P is evidence of conflicting reports, not proof both underlying
facts hold. Preserve source dependence and measurement error.

**Basis:** S7's logical distinction; S2's restraint about causal explanation.
Organizational paradox may mean persistent competing demands, not classical
logical inconsistency. The metadata-only organizational literature has not
been promoted to a case finding.

**Framework hypothesis:** Context-indexed comparison may reduce false
contradiction and deception attributions. That improvement is untested.

**Test:** Predefine context-matched and context-mismatched case pairs;
independent domain reviewers resolve them against source records. Compare
unsupported-attribution and missed-conflict rates with a provenance-only
baseline. Blind reviewers to method labels where feasible; retain disagreement
and uncertainty. Disconfirmation includes increased false accusations or no
measurable improvement.

## BOTTLENECK: conserved work and causal restraint

**Question:** What measured resource/coordination condition limits useful
throughput within this boundary?

Use `L = lambda * W`: L is mean tasks in the defined system, lambda mean task
arrival rate, W mean time in that system. Units must match. Little's original
abstract states finite means and stationary/ergodic arrival conditions; do not
silently apply this relationship to an unstable backlog or mismatched task
populations. Abandoned/rejected tasks and boundary crossings must be handled
consistently. Inspect variation and censoring, not just means.

Illustrative only: `lambda = 2 tasks/hour` and `W = 3 hours` imply
`L = 6 tasks` if assumptions hold. These are not repository measurements.
The equation is a relationship, not a bottleneck-location algorithm.
For a simple serial, no-bypass process with all capacities expressed in the
same work units, sustained throughput cannot exceed the smallest stage
capacity; parallelism, batching, rework and changing task mix need a different
model. This is an explicit framework model, not a quoted finding from S4.

**Basis:** S4 abstract-level queue theory; S2 causal/association distinction.
Neither long waits nor spare nominal resources identify WILL NOT or intent.

**Test:** Collect arrivals, departures, rejection/abandonment, queue size,
service/review time, utilization and task mix over a specified interval.
Compare targeted capacity/coordination changes using a defensible prospective
design. Record confounders, outages and censoring. Disconfirmation includes
unchanged throughput or displaced harm/bottlenecks. The human-release stage
is a real service-capacity constraint, not permission to remove the inquiry gate.

## DUAL LAYER: observation is not identification

**Question:** Which operational state is supported by observations, and which
remains an unidentifiable explanation of surface signals?

Specify an observation model `Y = h(Z, U) + error`, where Y is an observed
signal, Z a proposed latent state, U declared contextual variables, and h a
specified measurement mapping. This is a model template, not evidence that Z
exists or can be recovered.

A concrete binary measurement example:

```text
r = sensitivity * prevalence + (1 - specificity) * (1 - prevalence)
prevalence = (r + specificity - 1) / (sensitivity + specificity - 1)
```

The inversion needs independently known/stable sensitivity and specificity,
compatible population sampling, `sensitivity + specificity != 1`, and a result
within [0, 1]. Observed positive rate r alone does not identify all three
unknowns. Unknown error rates or selection bias leave the latent prevalence
unresolved. This elementary probability derivation is FRAMEWORK SYNTHESIS,
not an imported theorem validating hidden intent or human source conditions.

**Basis:** S1's uncertainty boundary and S2's modeling restraint. Organizational
decoupling is a bibliographic research candidate, not a confirmed diagnosis.

**Test:** Obtain independent calibration/operational observations, compare
multiple plausible latent models, and report sensitivity to error/selection.
Disconfirmation includes equally well-fitting alternatives, invalid calibration
or no observable improvement. Missing data must lower what can be concluded,
not become proof of concealment.

## XFACTOR: uncertainty, proper scoring and consequence

**Question:** What omitted scenario could change a decision, and how will its
forecast and consequence be tested?

For declared binary events, use the loss convention
`Brier = mean((p_i - y_i)^2)` with frozen `p_i in [0,1]` and resolved
`y_i in {0,1}`. Lower is better. Some multicategory/sign conventions differ;
declare the exact convention before comparison. Separate calibration from
sharpness and analytical confidence. Use the existing
[forecasting procedure](../VesselFramework_Forecasting_SKILL_v1.0.md), not a
new parallel forecast ledger.

**Conditional mathematical demonstration:** If Y is Bernoulli(q), a reported
probability p has expected squared loss
`E[(p-Y)^2] = (p-q)^2 + q*(1-q)`. Expansion gives
`p^2 - 2*p*q + q`; the minimum over p in [0,1] is uniquely at p=q.
This checkable conditional result explains honest probability elicitation.
It does not establish q from intuition, validate forecasts on unobserved
events, or prove VessellFramework forecasting superiority.

**Basis:** S3 proper-score framing. For decision analysis, use separately
declared losses such as `expected_loss(a) = sum(p_s * loss(a,s))`; those
probabilities/losses are assumptions or estimates, not facts created by
the formula. Worst-case bounds require a justified scenario set.

**Test:** Freeze questions/horizons/resolution rules/probabilities; score all
resolved events against a base-rate/simple baseline. Predefine treatment of
unresolved/ambiguous outcomes and correlated cases. Report uncertainty,
coverage, calibration, missed severe outcomes and changes in decisions.
Disconfirmation includes worse loss, hindsight selection or unresolvable claims.

## KNOWING FIELD: human inquiry, not machine consciousness

**Question:** How do observer participation, affected people, consent,
dissent and missing perspectives shape the inquiry and its consequences?

**Basis:** S6, fully reviewed, supports the human-led theoretical lens.
S5's reviewed abstract supplies a compatible human/technology/environment
unit of inquiry, not validation of S6 or this integration.
No physical field equation, Shannon entropy value, collective agreement or
complete JSON record measures presencing. The fifth-pillar release policy
is owner-selected documentary/authorization policy.

**Framework hypothesis:** Structured voluntary inquiry may improve detection
of missing perspectives and consequential errors. This has not been tested
with participants. Human reports establish reported experience, not its
ontology; no software-generated account can substitute for participation.

**Test:** With appropriate consent and study governance, evaluate predeclared
source-grounded omission/error rates, participant-reported usefulness/burden,
preserved dissent, review latency and adverse effects. Instruments themselves
need construct-validity review. A process-completeness score is a process
measure, not an awareness scale. Assess power asymmetry and differential
participation; never punish refusal or manufacture consensus.

## Prospective comparative and operational study

This study is **NOT PERFORMED**. No sample size, power estimate or efficacy
result is asserted.

1. Preregister domain, hypotheses, primary outcomes, baseline, recruitment,
   inclusion/exclusion, analysis and stop conditions. Justify sample size with
   pilot variability, expected effect and consequence of error; do not choose
   an arbitrary count and call it powered.
2. Start with synthetic/public held-out cases. Compare provenance-only
   assessment, four-pillar analysis and five-pillar analysis on equivalent
   evidence. Ablation outputs are research previews, never a route around
   mandatory human completion before live report release.
3. Freeze source snapshots, method versions, prompts, model/environment,
   case allocation and scoring conventions. Randomize/counterbalance as
   appropriate; account for repeated reviewers and correlated cases.
4. Have independent domain reviewers adjudicate source support with a
   documented rubric. Blinded coding and inter-rater disagreement characterize
   scoring reliability; agreement itself does not establish truth.
5. Measure unsupported consequential claims, source/claim trace quality,
   detected omissions and forecast loss where events are resolvable.
   Separately measure time, human burden, failure/rejection, costs, correction
   rates and adverse consequences. Avoid treating one composite score as
   all of these outcomes.
6. Publish effect estimates with design-appropriate uncertainty, missingness,
   limitations, null/adverse results and generalization bounds. A new site,
   domain or population needs a new external-validity assessment.
7. Preserve independent execution, consent and release authority. A live
   paid/multiuser pilot requires production identity/isolation work that the
   current single-operator stack has not completed.

The prior 783 Python, 14 workspace and 19 dashboard passing tests establish
software behavior in their test scope. They are not participant samples,
forecast-calibration trials or evidence of improved human decision outcomes.

## Research case study: "a SHA hash becomes crypto"

| Pillar | Finding applied | Comparative/operational outcome |
|---|---|---|
| PARADOX | Hash creation and protocol-paid work are different predicates. | Replaced the proposed automatic hash-to-money claim with conditional paid-service/accepted-work routes. No earnings measured. |
| BOTTLENECK | Buyers, reviewer capacity, settlement and demand are necessary stages. | Roadmap includes priced asynchronous jobs, review SLA, rejection/refund and demand gates. No service deployed. |
| DUAL LAYER | Marketplace listings and token narratives are surface signals; actual accepted jobs/net settlement need measurement. | No registration, listed price or testnet points counted as revenue. |
| XFACTOR | Costs, volatility, protocol changes, unavailable subnets and privacy failure can dominate returns. | No profitability forecast; explicit uncertainty and owner-approved financial limits before any experiment. |
| KNOWING FIELD | Owner/reviewers/buyers/affected source subjects have different interests and consent boundaries. | Payment cannot complete human inquiry or confer release/execution authority; public commitments exclude private source content. |

Research also rejected unverified search citations, left inaccessible theories
as candidates, and corrected the published setup workflow's Python-version
mismatch. These are documentary/software corrections, not proof of scientific
efficacy. The [blockchain roadmap](blockchain-agent-economy-roadmap.md) is the
persisted operational plan, not an implemented monetary system.

## Digital evidence: what can be proved now

The repository's [SHA manifest](../VessellFramework_v3.8.1_SHA256_Manifest.json)
and [verifier](../verify_manifest.py) provide byte-integrity checks relative
to that manifest. Current ambient source/lifecycle/filing/inquiry hashes bind
records and detect specified drift. They are unsigned local records, not
independent attestations against an administrator rewriting all state.
GitHub publication provides a retrievable version; it is not a blockchain
timestamp, independent replication or validated theory.

A digital dossier should preserve the exact claim, sources/access levels,
model/assumptions, test plan/results, uncertainty, artifacts/environment,
digests, corrections and verification status. Later, an independently
verified timestamp may establish a prior-existence bound; a signature may
establish key authorization with a verified identity binding; repeatable
computation may establish reproducibility. Each supports a different claim.
None upgrades unsupported empirical/causal/theoretical assertions.

**Current boundary:** No universal per-invocation signed receipt, Merkle batch,
external timestamp proof, chain attestation, wallet, payment adapter or mining
reward exists in this release. The new skill supplies a dossier template and
research method; it does not add a machine-enforced scientific output schema.
Original source bytes and historical hash contracts remain unchanged.

## References (APA 7)

Gneiting, T., & Raftery, A. E. (2007). Strictly proper scoring rules, prediction,
and estimation. *Journal of the American Statistical Association, 102*(477),
359-378. https://doi.org/10.1198/016214506000001437

Hollan, J., Hutchins, E., & Kirsh, D. (2000). Distributed cognition: Toward a
new foundation for human-computer interaction research. *ACM Transactions on
Computer-Human Interaction, 7*(2), 174-196. https://doi.org/10.1145/353485.353487
[Abstract/metadata reviewed.]

Little, J. D. C. (1961). A proof for the queuing formula: L = lambda W.
*Operations Research, 9*(3), 383-387. https://doi.org/10.1287/opre.9.3.383
[Abstract/metadata reviewed; formula transliterated to ASCII.]

National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2015). *Secure hash standard
(SHS)* (FIPS PUB 180-4). https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.FIPS.180-4
[Publication record reviewed.]

National Institute of Standards and Technology. (2023). *Artificial intelligence
risk management framework (AI RMF 1.0)* (NIST AI 100-1).
https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.100-1 [Overview reviewed.]

Pearl, J. (2009). Causal inference in statistics: An overview.
*Statistics Surveys, 3*, 96-146. https://doi.org/10.1214/09-SS057

*Journal of Awareness-Based Systems Change, 4*(1), 19-48.
https://doi.org/10.47061/jasc.v4i1.7909

*The Bell System Technical Journal, 27*(3), 379-423.
https://doi.org/10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x
[The reviewed reprint also contains the continuation, 27(4), 623-656.]

name: vessel-framework-knowing-field
description: >
  Applies KNOWING FIELD, the fifth pillar, across the original four analytical
  pillars with human-led perspective inquiry, provenance and mandatory
  source-bound human completion before report release.
---

# VessellFramework Knowing Field: Fifth-Pillar Integration Skill

## Version and status

Version 0.1, October 7, 2026. OWNER-AUTHORIZED POLICY /
RESEARCH ADAPTATION / CALIBRATION PENDING.
Created with the [Skill Creator](VesselFramework_Skill_Creator_SKILL_v0.1.md)
after applying the [theory skill](Knowing_Field_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md) in the
[framework audit](docs/knowing-field-framework-audit.md).
Runtime implementation validates records and authority, not presencing.

## Scientific and digital-evidence handoff

Apply [Scientific Evidence](VesselFramework_Scientific_Evidence_SKILL_v0.1.md)
and its [historical five-pillar dossier and current reciprocal six-pillar extension](docs/pillar-scientific-foundations.md).
Keep mathematical assumptions, observed associations, causal identification,
human accounts and empirical outcomes distinct. Use the dossier template
without claiming a new runtime schema or validated theory.
Human inquiry/release hashes bind documentary records; they do not certify
experience. The [payment/anchoring roadmap](docs/blockchain-agent-economy-roadmap.md)
is prospective and cannot convert a receipt, payment or consensus into human
completion, release approval or execution authority.

## Purpose and authority

For prompt-trajectory audits, keep the owner's explicit self-report, visible
assistant output, analyst synthesis, and any independently observed result as
separate perspectives with separate provenance. Record revision history and
missing turns; do not translate a prompt sequence into a claim about the
owner's private mental state or a generated rationale into access to model
internals. Apply the protocol in
[`docs/prompt-steering-and-reasoning-audit.md`](docs/prompt-steering-and-reasoning-audit.md).

The current architecture also includes
[GAME THEORY as its sixth pillar](VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md).
Declared incentives and conditional solver output inform inquiry, never
replace human perspective accounts or satisfy this release gate.

KNOWING FIELD asks: **How do the observer, affected participants, relationships,
absent perspectives and emerging possibilities shape this analysis and its
consequences, and who may legitimately act?**

It complements rather than displaces PARADOX, BOTTLENECK, DUAL LAYER and
XFACTOR. Harm Gate, Evidence Assurance, Provenance Firewall and author-source
preservation retain precedence. The policy requires a human-completed fifth
pillar before any new human report release, including pending legacy jobs.
No retrospective rewriting or automatic assessment of historical releases.

## Sixth-pillar strategic-model bridge

Use the [GAME THEORY skill](VesselFramework_Game_Theory_SKILL_v0.1.md) and
[audit](docs/game-theory-framework-audit.md) for the strategic-model handoff.
Human field inquiry informs model boundaries and participant coverage,
observer position and model choices, declared assumptions, and interpretation
of conditional outputs. Record affected people outside the modeled actors,
missing or declined perspectives, participation consent and dissent; do not
turn unavailable accounts into inferred preferences or agreement. Keep human
accounts distinct from modeled actors, actions, information and utilities.

This bridge is VessellFramework synthesis, not an external validation claim.
Game-theory outputs do not substitute for human inquiry, create consent, infer
motives, raise confidence or validate outcomes. They cannot bypass human
completion bound to the actual source and exact preview, the separate human
release decision, Harm Gate or execution authority.

## Source adoption and modification

Scharmer and Pomeroy (2024), *Fourth person: The knowing of the field*,
https://doi.org/10.47061/jasc.v4i1.7909, pp. 19-48, provide the external lens.
Full coverage and PDF fingerprint are in the theory skill.
Their article is an action-research-informed epistemological proposal and
explicitly distinguishes embodied presencing from generative AI capability.
The five phenomena are not software metrics.

The mandatory human completion gate, structured record, source binding,
revision rules and cross-pillar integration are **VessellFramework synthesis**,
not requirements of the paper or independently validated science.
Human reflection may be absent or declined. Documentation of limitations
counts as honest inquiry, not as a finding that all perspectives were accessed.

## Triggers, non-triggers and input contract

Apply to analytical framing, report preparation/release, doctrine revision,
workflow design and significant human-agent decisions. Mechanical substeps
may reuse an enclosing assessment; never use this skill to bypass other gates.
It is not a personality, consciousness, spirituality or consensus detector.

Machine contract: [field-inquiry schema](schemas/field-inquiry.schema.json).
Required: bounded context; observer position; affected parties and participation
state; distinct accounts of the four perspectives; evidence references;
dissent; blind spots; attention; intention; agency; alternatives;
evaluation plan; limitations.
Explicit unavailable/declined accounts are preferable to invented experiences.
Consent applies to inquiry participation, not to fabricated group agreement.

## Sequence and cross-pillar handoffs

`QUESTION -> FIELD BOUNDARY / OBSERVER -> SIGNAL -> PROVENANCE -> PERSPECTIVES
-> PARADOX -> BOTTLENECK -> DUAL LAYER -> XFACTOR -> KNOWING FIELD SYNTHESIS
-> ALTERNATIVES -> AUTHORITY -> CONSEQUENCE -> CONFIDENCE -> HARM GATE
-> HUMAN FIELD COMPLETION -> HUMAN RELEASE DECISION -> EVALUATION`

| Pillar | Required field-aware handoff |
|---|---|
| PARADOX | Distinguish contradiction from different collection positions, interpretive frames and omitted voices. |
| BOTTLENECK | Examine coordination, exclusion and constitutive constraints before assigning incapacity or unwillingness. |
| DUAL LAYER | Distinguish observable manifestation from proposed source conditions; disclose the analyst's intervention. |
| XFACTOR | Convert emergent possibilities into bounded alternatives and disconfirmers, not forecasts or action grants. |
| KNOWING FIELD | Integrate observer participation, perspective gaps, dissent and attention/intention/agency into a documented, correctable human assessment. |
| GAME THEORY | Use human inquiry to bound strategic models and participant coverage, disclose observer/model choices and assumptions, and interpret conditional outputs without replacing missing accounts, consent or dissent. |

1. Read the theory skill; scope the relevant human/system field.
2. Preserve provenance and mark source reports versus interpretations.
3. Invite voluntary reflection/dialogue when appropriate; preserve refusal.
4. Apply original diagnostics only where they add value; do not force every
   pillar into every small task.
5. Record relational blind spots, alternatives, intended agency and limitations.
6. Assess consequences for operator, other affected people and wider systems.
7. An authorized human completes the bounded inquiry against the actual
   input/preview, with optimistic concurrency and durable audit.
8. Separately decide release under Harm Gate and existing authority.
9. Monitor outcomes; correction invalidates assumptions and requires a new
   version/assessment rather than erasing prior evidence.

## Decision and output contract

Outputs include six-pillar framing, inquiry status, source-linked assessment,
unresolved limitations, human completion actor/time/bindings, and next test.
Machine validation means DOCUMENTED_UNREVIEWED, not HUMAN_COMPLETED.
Human completion means procedural completion, not truth or field experience.
Missing inquiry blocks release but not collection, preview, rejection,
diagnostics or preservation. Historical results remain identifiable as legacy.
No waiver through folder metadata, caller declarations or owner task dispatch.

## Failures, harm and adversarial tests

Block release for missing human completion, stale input/preview binding,
invalid evidence IDs, tampered history, stale assessment revision or Harm Gate
failure. Reject unknown fields, unsupported experience claims as machine
capabilities and injected approval/authority fields.
Preserve dissent even after completion; do not equate agreement with consent.

Test T1-T10 from the Skill Creator and specifically:
agent cannot self-complete; sparse input remains incomplete; declined voices
stay declined; shared roots stay shared; alternate explanation can win;
legacy approval returns to review; completion cannot bypass harm;
filing never completes inquiry; specialist/capture/push reuse one contract;
no second confidence algorithm is created.

## Calibration, change record and runtime state

Creation is policy adoption, not empirical promotion. Prospective calibration
must compare blind-spot identification, burden, delay, error and consequence
against a declared baseline in consented human studies.
No efficacy or machine phenomenology claim follows from tests.
Canonical runtime status is demonstrated by tests and installed-package
validation, not the existence of these Markdown instructions.
Software integration in 3.12.0 is verified by the
[audit's implementation record](docs/knowing-field-framework-audit.md#implemented-software-verification-3120):
783 Python tests, 14 workspace tests, 19 public-dashboard tests, strict
runtime typing, built/installed package and synthetic HTTP/browser review.
This is procedural software evidence, not promotion of the theory through
human outcome measurements. The human completion gate is policy, not a
